docs.title: PyAlloq
docs.text: A modern Python SDK for quantitative portfolio optimization. Build, backtest, and iterate on any portfolio strategy using a fully modular, plug-and-play architecture.

docs.title: What is PyAlloq?
docs.text:
PyAlloq is a research-grade SDK that gives you all the building blocks you need to go from raw market data to a fully backtested, production-ready portfolio strategy — without writing boilerplate.

Every component is independently swappable. Change your covariance estimator. Try a different allocator. Add a new return estimator. Your backtesting engine stays the same.

from pyalloq_data_connector.yahoo_finance import YahooFinanceClient
from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.risk_parity import RiskParityAllocator
from pyalloq_core.pipeline import StrategyPipeline
from pyalloq_backtest.engine import WalkForwardEngine

data = YahooFinanceClient().get_market_data(
    tickers=["AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "AMZN", "TSLA"],
    start="2020-01-01", end="2024-01-01"
)

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(allocator=RiskParityAllocator(tickers=data.assets))
results  = WalkForwardEngine(pipeline=pipeline).run(data)

print(results["tear_sheet"])

docs.title: Feature Highlights
docs.text:
• 🎯 5 classical allocators: Equal Weight, Markowitz (Min Vol / Max Sharpe / Max Return), Risk Parity, Risk Budgeting, Max Diversification
  • 🌳 3 graph-based ML allocators: HRP, HERC, NCO — no covariance inversion required
  • 📈 6 return estimators: EWMA, Momentum, Factor, James-Stein, Implied, Black-Litterman
  • 📊 5 covariance estimators: Empirical, EWMA, Ledoit-Wolf, RMT Denoising, Semi-Covariance
  • 🎲 5 Monte Carlo scenario generators: Gaussian, PCA Factor, Filtered Historical Simulation (FHS), GARCH-EVT-Student-\(t\) Copula, and GMM Markov Regimes
  • 🔭 Meucci Entropy Pooling: First- and second-moment views (AbsoluteView, RelativeView, VolatilityView, CovarianceView) with path-dependent CVaR, View-Adjusted MDD, and Probability of Ruin
  • 🔁 4 backtest splitters & validation engines: Rolling Window, Expanding Window, Purged K-Fold, plus Combinatorial Purged CV (CPCVSplitter) and Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBOEvaluator)
  • 🎨 4 interactive visualization Tear Sheets (pyalloq-viz): Multiverse & Simulation, Robustness & Overfitting (PBO/CPCV), Macro Regime & Entropy, and Allocation Mechanics & Risk
  • 💸 2 transaction cost models: Flat Bps, Almgren-Chriss market impact
  • 🔬 Zero-lookahead guarantee via MarketData.validate_alignment() and slice_time()

docs.title: split
docs.text:
split(
    data: MarketData,
) -> Generator[tuple[MarketData, MarketData], None, None]

Yields (train_data, test_data) for neural network training.

Source code in src/pyalloq-backtest/src/pyalloq_backtest/splitters.py 
def split(
    self, data: MarketData
) -> Generator[tuple[MarketData, MarketData], None, None]:
    """Yields (train_data, test_data) for neural network training."""

    total_length = len(data.prices)
    fold_size = total_length // self.n_splits
    embargo_size = int(total_length * self.embargo_pct)

    indices = np.arange(total_length)
    dates = data.prices.index

    for i in range(self.n_splits):
        test_start = i * fold_size
        test_end = test_start + fold_size if i < self.n_splits - 1 else total_length

        test_indices = indices[test_start:test_end]
        train_indices_left = indices[: max(0, test_start - embargo_size)]
        train_indices_right = indices[min(total_length, test_end + embargo_size) :]

        train_indices = np.concatenate([train_indices_left, train_indices_right])

        if len(train_indices) == 0:
            continue

        train_dates = dates[train_indices]
        test_dates = dates[test_indices]

        train_data = MarketData(
            prices=data.prices.loc[train_dates],
            features={k: v.loc[train_dates] for k, v in data.features.items()}
            if data.features
            else {},
            cross_sectional=data.cross_sectional,
            risk_free_rate=data.risk_free_rate.loc[train_dates]
            if isinstance(data.risk_free_rate, pd.Series)
            else data.risk_free_rate,
        )

        test_data = MarketData(
            prices=data.prices.loc[test_dates],
            features={k: v.loc[test_dates] for k, v in data.features.items()}
            if data.features
            else {},
            cross_sectional=data.cross_sectional,
            risk_free_rate=data.risk_free_rate.loc[test_dates]
            if isinstance(data.risk_free_rate, pd.Series)
            else data.risk_free_rate,
        )

        yield train_data, test_data

docs.title: CPCVSplitter
docs.text:
CPCVSplitter(
    n_groups: int = 6,
    k_test_groups: int = 2,
    purge_pct: float = 0.01,
    embargo_pct: float = 0.01,
    max_paths: int = 250,
    random_state: int | None = 42,
)

Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV) & Regime Block Scrambling engine.

Supports two workflows: 1. .split(data): Yields (train_data, test_data, test_group_indices) across all C(n_groups, k_test_groups) splits with purge and embargo zones applied. 2. .scramble_returns(returns) / .scramble_backtest(backtest_result): Partitions a historical return series into n_groups chronological regime blocks and recombines them into n_paths combinatorial timelines (scrambling the chronological order of market regimes) to test path-dependent survival (drawdowns, compounding, ruin) when regime sequences are reordered.

Source code in src/pyalloq-backtest/src/pyalloq_backtest/overfitting.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    n_groups: int = 6,
    k_test_groups: int = 2,
    purge_pct: float = 0.01,
    embargo_pct: float = 0.01,
    max_paths: int = 250,
    random_state: int | None = 42,
) -> None:
    if n_groups < 2:
        raise ValueError("`n_groups` must be >= 2.")
    if not (1 <= k_test_groups < n_groups):
        raise ValueError("`k_test_groups` must be between 1 and `n_groups - 1`.")
    self.n_groups = n_groups
    self.k_test_groups = k_test_groups
    self.purge_pct = purge_pct
    self.embargo_pct = embargo_pct
    self.max_paths = max_paths
    self.random_state = random_state

docs.title: split
docs.text:
split(
    data: MarketData,
) -> list[tuple[MarketData, MarketData, tuple[int, ...]]]

Generates all C(N, k) purged & embargoed train/test splits of MarketData.

Source code in src/pyalloq-backtest/src/pyalloq_backtest/overfitting.py 
def split(
    self, data: MarketData
) -> list[tuple[MarketData, MarketData, tuple[int, ...]]]:
    """
    Generates all C(N, k) purged & embargoed train/test splits of MarketData.
    """
    total_length = len(data.prices)
    indices = np.arange(total_length)
    groups = np.array_split(indices, self.n_groups)
    purge_size = int(total_length * self.purge_pct)
    embargo_size = int(total_length * self.embargo_pct)
    dates = data.prices.index

    splits_out: list[tuple[MarketData, MarketData, tuple[int, ...]]] = []

    for test_group_ids in combinations(range(self.n_groups), self.k_test_groups):
        test_mask = np.zeros(total_length, dtype=bool)
        banned_mask = np.zeros(total_length, dtype=bool)

        for gid in test_group_ids:
            g_idx = groups[gid]
            if len(g_idx) == 0:
                continue
            test_mask[g_idx] = True
            start_i = max(0, int(g_idx[0]) - purge_size)
            end_i = min(total_length, int(g_idx[-1]) + 1 + embargo_size)
            banned_mask[start_i:end_i] = True

        train_mask = ~banned_mask
        train_dates = dates[train_mask]
        test_dates = dates[test_mask]

        if len(train_dates) == 0 or len(test_dates) == 0:
            continue

        train_data = MarketData(
            prices=data.prices.loc[train_dates],
            features={k: v.loc[train_dates] for k, v in data.features.items()}
            if data.features
            else {},
            cross_sectional=data.cross_sectional,
            risk_free_rate=data.risk_free_rate.loc[train_dates]
            if isinstance(data.risk_free_rate, pd.Series)
            else data.risk_free_rate,
        )
        test_data = MarketData(
            prices=data.prices.loc[test_dates],
            features={k: v.loc[test_dates] for k, v in data.features.items()}
            if data.features
            else {},
            cross_sectional=data.cross_sectional,
            risk_free_rate=data.risk_free_rate.loc[test_dates]
            if isinstance(data.risk_free_rate, pd.Series)
            else data.risk_free_rate,
        )
        splits_out.append((train_data, test_data, test_group_ids))

    return splits_out

docs.title: assemble_cpcv_paths
docs.text:
assemble_cpcv_paths(
    oos_split_returns: dict[tuple[int, ...], Series],
    historical_returns: Series | None = None,
    risk_free_rate: float = 0.0,
) -> CPCVResult

Reconstructs the phi(N, k) = C(N - 1, k - 1) full-horizon out-of-sample backtest paths from the C(N, k) test split evaluations according to Lopez de Prado (2018).

Source code in src/pyalloq-backtest/src/pyalloq_backtest/overfitting.py 
def assemble_cpcv_paths(
    self,
    oos_split_returns: dict[tuple[int, ...], pd.Series],
    historical_returns: pd.Series | None = None,
    risk_free_rate: float = 0.0,
) -> CPCVResult:
    """
    Reconstructs the phi(N, k) = C(N - 1, k - 1) full-horizon out-of-sample backtest paths
    from the C(N, k) test split evaluations according to Lopez de Prado (2018).
    """
    group_appearances: dict[int, list[pd.Series]] = {
        g: [] for g in range(self.n_groups)
    }

    # Sort splits lexicographically so path assignment is deterministic
    for test_group_ids in sorted(oos_split_returns.keys()):
        split_ret = oos_split_returns[test_group_ids]
        # Split the test return series evenly across its k test groups
        group_slices = np.array_split(
            np.arange(len(split_ret)), len(test_group_ids)
        )
        for gid, idx_slice in zip(test_group_ids, group_slices):
            group_appearances[gid].append(split_ret.iloc[idx_slice])

    n_paths = min(len(v) for v in group_appearances.values() if len(v) > 0)
    path_series_list: list[pd.Series] = []
    block_orders: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []

    for p_idx in range(n_paths):
        segments = [group_appearances[g][p_idx] for g in range(self.n_groups)]
        combined = pd.concat(segments).sort_index()
        combined.name = f"CPCV_Path_{p_idx}"
        path_series_list.append(combined)
        block_orders.append(tuple(range(self.n_groups)))

    returns_df = pd.concat(path_series_list, axis=1).dropna(how="all").fillna(0.0)
    return self._build_cpcv_result(
        returns_df,
        block_orders=block_orders,
        historical_returns=historical_returns,
        risk_free_rate=risk_free_rate,
    )

docs.title: scramble_timelines
docs.text:
scramble_timelines(
    source: BacktestResult | Series,
    risk_free_rate: float = 0.0,
    block_bootstrap: bool = True,
) -> CPCVResult

Partitions historical strategy returns into n_groups regime blocks and generates combinatorial scrambled timelines (permutations + block-resampled paths with subtle within-block jitter/subsampling) to evaluate strategy survival across scrambled chronological sequences of market regimes.

Source code in src/pyalloq-backtest/src/pyalloq_backtest/overfitting.py 
def scramble_timelines(
    self,
    source: BacktestResult | pd.Series,
    risk_free_rate: float = 0.0,
    block_bootstrap: bool = True,
) -> CPCVResult:
    """
    Partitions historical strategy returns into `n_groups` regime blocks and generates
    combinatorial scrambled timelines (permutations + block-resampled paths with subtle
    within-block jitter/subsampling) to evaluate strategy survival across scrambled
    chronological sequences of market regimes.
    """
    if isinstance(source, BacktestResult):
        hist_returns = source.returns.dropna()
    else:
        hist_returns = pd.Series(source).dropna()

    rng = np.random.default_rng(self.random_state)
    ret_vals = hist_returns.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    blocks = np.array_split(ret_vals, self.n_groups)
    n_total = len(ret_vals)

    # Generate distinct block sequences (combinatorial permutations + bootstrap block draws)
    all_orders: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
    if self.n_groups <= 6:
        from itertools import permutations

        perms = list(permutations(range(self.n_groups)))
        # Exclude identity as path 0 if we want pure scrambled, or include all
        if len(perms) > self.max_paths:
            chosen_idx = rng.choice(len(perms), size=self.max_paths, replace=False)
            all_orders = [perms[i] for i in chosen_idx]
        else:
            all_orders = perms
    else:
        seen: set[tuple[int, ...]] = set()
        for _ in range(self.max_paths * 3):
            if len(all_orders) >= self.max_paths:
                break
            if block_bootstrap:
                order = tuple(
                    int(x)
                    for x in rng.choice(
                        self.n_groups, size=self.n_groups, replace=True
                    )
                )
            else:
                order = tuple(int(x) for x in rng.permutation(self.n_groups))
            if order not in seen:
                seen.add(order)
                all_orders.append(order)

    scrambled_cols: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    for idx, order in enumerate(all_orders):
        recombined = np.concatenate([blocks[b] for b in order])
        if block_bootstrap and idx > 0:
            # Apply circular shift within each block so paths aren't identical in terminal return
            shifted_blocks = []
            for b in order:
                blk = blocks[b]
                if len(blk) > 2:
                    shift = int(rng.integers(0, len(blk)))
                    # Sample with replacement 90% + permutation to vary compounding & Sharpe slightly
                    sub_idx = rng.choice(len(blk), size=len(blk), replace=True)
                    blk = np.roll(blk, shift) if idx % 2 == 0 else blk[sub_idx]
                shifted_blocks.append(blk)
            recombined = np.concatenate(shifted_blocks)

        # Align length to n_total
        if len(recombined) >= n_total:
            recombined = recombined[:n_total]
        else:
            pad = np.zeros(n_total - len(recombined))
            recombined = np.concatenate([recombined, pad])

        scrambled_cols[f"Path_{idx}"] = recombined

    returns_df = pd.DataFrame(scrambled_cols, index=hist_returns.index)
    return self._build_cpcv_result(
        returns_df,
        block_orders=all_orders,
        historical_returns=hist_returns,
        risk_free_rate=risk_free_rate,
    )

Calculates exact PBO via Combinatorial Symmetric Cross-Validation (CSCV) across M trials.

Source code in src/pyalloq-backtest/src/pyalloq_backtest/overfitting.py 
def evaluate_cscv(
    self,
    strategy_returns: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray | Sequence[BacktestResult],
) -> PBOResult:
    """
    Calculates exact PBO via Combinatorial Symmetric Cross-Validation (CSCV) across M trials.
    """
    if isinstance(strategy_returns, pd.DataFrame):
        M_mat = (
            strategy_returns.dropna(how="all")
            .fillna(0.0)
            .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        )
    elif isinstance(strategy_returns, np.ndarray):
        M_mat = np.asarray(strategy_returns, dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        df_concat = pd.concat(
            [
                res.returns.rename(f"{res.name}_{i}")
                for i, res in enumerate(strategy_returns)
            ],
            axis=1,
        ).fillna(0.0)
        M_mat = df_concat.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)

    if M_mat.ndim != 2 or M_mat.shape[1] < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "CSCV requires a 2D return matrix of shape (T, M) with at least M >= 2 strategy trials."
        )

    T, M_trials = M_mat.shape
    S = min(self.n_partitions, (T // 5) * 2)
    S = max(2, S - (S % 2))

    submatrices = np.array_split(M_mat, S, axis=0)
    half_S = S // 2
    all_indices = set(range(S))

    logits_list: list[float] = []
    is_sharpes_list: list[float] = []
    oos_sharpes_list: list[float] = []

    for is_group_tuple in combinations(range(S), half_S):
        oos_group_tuple = tuple(sorted(all_indices - set(is_group_tuple)))
        J_is = np.vstack([submatrices[i] for i in is_group_tuple])
        J_oos = np.vstack([submatrices[i] for i in oos_group_tuple])

        R_is = self._annualized_sharpes(J_is, self.risk_free_rate)
        R_oos = self._annualized_sharpes(J_oos, self.risk_free_rate)

        best_m = int(np.argmax(R_is))
        is_best_sr = float(R_is[best_m])
        oos_of_best_sr = float(R_oos[best_m])

        # Relative rank of the IS-optimal strategy in OOS (in (0, 1))
        less_count = float(np.sum(R_oos < oos_of_best_sr))
        equal_count = float(np.sum(R_oos == oos_of_best_sr))
        omega_c = (less_count + 0.5 * equal_count) / float(M_trials)
        omega_c = float(
            np.clip(omega_c, 1.0 / (2.0 * M_trials), 1.0 - 1.0 / (2.0 * M_trials))
        )

        logit = math.log(omega_c / (1.0 - omega_c))
        logits_list.append(logit)
        is_sharpes_list.append(is_best_sr)
        oos_sharpes_list.append(oos_of_best_sr)

    logits_arr = np.asarray(logits_list, dtype=np.float64)
    is_arr = np.asarray(is_sharpes_list, dtype=np.float64)
    oos_arr = np.asarray(oos_sharpes_list, dtype=np.float64)

    pbo = float(np.mean(logits_arr <= 0.0))
    prob_loss = float(np.mean(oos_arr < 0.0))

    if len(is_arr) > 1 and np.std(is_arr) > 1e-12:
        slope, intercept = np.polyfit(is_arr, oos_arr, 1)
    else:
        slope, intercept = 0.0, float(np.mean(oos_arr))

    full_sharpes = self._annualized_sharpes(M_mat, self.risk_free_rate)
    best_overall_sharpe = float(np.max(full_sharpes))

    return PBOResult(
        pbo=pbo,
        logits=logits_arr,
        is_sharpes=is_arr,
        oos_sharpes=oos_arr,
        prob_oos_loss=prob_loss,
        degradation_slope=float(slope),
        degradation_intercept=float(intercept),
        historical_sharpe=best_overall_sharpe,
        mode="cscv",
    )

def evaluate_benchmark(
    self,
    historical: BacktestResult | pd.Series | float,
    synthetic: MonteCarloResult | CPCVResult | pd.Series | np.ndarray,
) -> PBOResult:
    """
    Evaluates how a single strategy's historical Sharpe compares to a synthetic
    (`MonteCarloResult`) or combinatorial (`CPCVResult`) Sharpe distribution.
    """
    if isinstance(historical, BacktestResult):
        if "sharpe_ratio" in historical.tear_sheet.index:
            val = historical.tear_sheet.loc["sharpe_ratio", "Value"]
            hist_sr = float(val)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        else:
            hist_sr = float(
                self._annualized_sharpes(
                    historical.returns.to_numpy()[:, None], self.risk_free_rate
                )[0]
            )
    elif isinstance(historical, pd.Series):
        hist_sr = float(
            self._annualized_sharpes(
                historical.dropna().to_numpy()[:, None], self.risk_free_rate
            )[0]
        )
    else:
        hist_sr = float(historical)

    if isinstance(synthetic, MonteCarloResult):
        if "sharpe_ratio" in synthetic.metrics_distribution.columns:
            sim_srs = synthetic.metrics_distribution["sharpe_ratio"].to_numpy(
                dtype=np.float64
            )
        else:
            sim_srs = self._annualized_sharpes(
                synthetic.returns_matrix.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
                self.risk_free_rate,
            )
    elif isinstance(synthetic, CPCVResult):
        sim_srs = synthetic.sharpe_ratios.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    elif isinstance(synthetic, pd.Series):
        sim_srs = synthetic.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        sim_srs = np.asarray(synthetic, dtype=np.float64)

    sim_srs = sim_srs[np.isfinite(sim_srs)]
    if len(sim_srs) == 0:
        sim_srs = np.array([0.0])

    # In single-strategy benchmark mode, overfitting risk is the probability mass of
    # synthetic/scrambled realizations falling below the historical Sharpe (or < 0),
    # and we also compute centered rank logits around the median synthetic Sharpe.
    pbo = float(np.mean(sim_srs < 0.0))
    prob_loss = float(np.mean(sim_srs < 0.0))

    ranks = (np.argsort(np.argsort(sim_srs)) + 0.5) / len(sim_srs)
    logits = np.log(ranks / (1.0 - ranks))
    is_srs = np.full_like(sim_srs, hist_sr)

    return PBOResult(
        pbo=pbo,
        logits=logits,
        is_sharpes=is_srs,
        oos_sharpes=sim_srs,
        prob_oos_loss=prob_loss,
        degradation_slope=0.0,
        degradation_intercept=float(np.mean(sim_srs)),
        historical_sharpe=hist_sr,
        mode="benchmark",
    )

def validate_alignment(self) -> None:
    """
    Ensures Time Series Data aligns perfectly to prevent look-ahead bias.
    """
    for feat_name, df_feat in self.features.items():
        if not self.prices.index.equals(df_feat.index):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Data misalignment: Feature: {feat_name} index does not perfectly match 'prices' index."
            )

    for feat_name, df_feat in self.future_features.items():
        if not self.prices.index.equals(df_feat.index):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Data misaligment: Future feature '{feat_name}' is missing historical dates."
            )

    if isinstance(self.risk_free_rate, pd.Series):
        if not self.prices.index.equals(self.risk_free_rate.index):
            raise ValueError(
                "Data misalignment: 'risk_free_rate' series index does not perfectly match 'prices' index."
            )

def slice_time(
    self,
    end_date: pd.Timestamp,
    lookback: int | None = None,
    horizon_steps: int = 0,
) -> "MarketData":
    """
    Returns a new MarketData instance safely sliced for a backtest window.
    """
    sliced_prices = self.prices.loc[:end_date]
    if lookback is not None:
        sliced_prices = sliced_prices.iloc[-lookback:]

    sliced_features: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    for name, feat in self.features.items():
        sliced_feat = feat.loc[:end_date]
        if lookback is not None:
            sliced_feat = sliced_feat.iloc[-lookback:]
        sliced_features[name] = sliced_feat

    sliced_futures: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    for name, feat in self.future_features.items():
        if end_date in feat.index:
            loc = feat.index.get_loc(end_date)
            if not isinstance(loc, int):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Duplicate timestamps found in future_features['{name}']"
                    "Time series indices must be strictly unique."
                )
            start_loc = max(0, (loc - lookback + 1)) if lookback else 0
            end_loc = loc + 1 + horizon_steps
            sliced_futures[name] = feat.iloc[start_loc:end_loc]
        else:
            sliced_futures[name] = feat.loc[:end_date]

    sliced_rf = self.risk_free_rate
    if isinstance(self.risk_free_rate, pd.Series):
        sliced_rf = self.risk_free_rate.loc[:end_date]
        if lookback is not None:
            sliced_rf = sliced_rf.iloc[-lookback:]

    return self.__class__(
        prices=sliced_prices,
        features=sliced_features,
        future_features=sliced_futures,
        cross_sectional=self.cross_sectional,
        risk_free_rate=sliced_rf,
    )

def get_cumulative_returns(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Returns total cumulative asset returns of shape (M, N) over the full horizon,
    incorporating t=0 initial_prices when available.
    """
    final_prices = self.prices[:, -1, :]
    if self.initial_prices is not None:
        init_p = np.asarray(self.initial_prices, dtype=final_prices.dtype)
        return (final_prices - init_p) / init_p
    initial_prices = self.prices[:, 0, :]
    return (final_prices - initial_prices) / initial_prices

def get_path(
    self, path_idx: int, feature_pipeline: object | None = None
) -> MarketData:
    """
    Slices the 3D tensor at index `path_idx` and returns a standard 2D MarketData
    object mathematically compatible with the existing StrategyPipeline.
    """
    path_prices = pd.DataFrame(
        self.prices[path_idx], index=self.timestamps, columns=self.asset_names
    )

    path_features: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    for feature_name, feature_tensor in self.features.items():
        # Support for both asset-specific features (M, T, N) and exogenous macro features (M, T, K)
        if feature_tensor.ndim == 3 and feature_tensor.shape[0] == self.n_paths:
            if feature_name in self.feature_columns:
                columns: list[str] | None = self.feature_columns[feature_name]
            elif feature_tensor.shape[2] == self.n_assets:
                columns = self.asset_names
            else:
                columns = None
            path_features[feature_name] = pd.DataFrame(
                feature_tensor[path_idx], index=self.timestamps, columns=columns
            )

    market_data = MarketData(prices=path_prices, features=path_features)
    if feature_pipeline is not None and hasattr(feature_pipeline, "run"):
        market_data = getattr(feature_pipeline, "run")(market_data)
    return market_data

def generate_batches(
    self, n_paths: int, horizon: int, batch_size: int = 1000
) -> Iterator[ScenarioMarketData]:
    """
    Yields simulated ScenarioMarketData in memory-bounded batches.
    """
    if batch_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError("batch_size must be a positive integer.")
    remaining = n_paths
    while remaining > 0:
        current_batch = min(batch_size, remaining)
        yield self.generate(n_paths=current_batch, horizon=horizon)
        remaining -= current_batch

docs.text:
get_market_data(
    tickers: list[str], start: datetime, end: datetime
) -> MarketData

The orchestrator method. Standardizes whatever chaotic data the vendor returns into mathematically pure T x N matrices, perfectly aligned in time.

Source code in src/pyalloq-data-connector/src/pyalloq_data_connector/base.py 
def get_market_data(
    self,
    tickers: list[str],
    start: dt.datetime,
    end: dt.datetime,
) -> MarketData:
    """
    The orchestrator method. Standardizes whatever chaotic data the vendor
    returns into mathematically pure T x N matrices, perfectly aligned in time.
    """
    raw_dict = self.fetch_raw_data(tickers, start, end)

    closes, volumes, opens, highs, lows = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}
    all_dates = pd.DatetimeIndex([])

    for ticker, df in raw_dict.items():
        df.columns = [str(c).lower() for c in df.columns]

        closes[ticker] = df.get("close", df.get("adj close"))
        if "volume" in df.columns:
            volumes[ticker] = df["volume"]
        if "open" in df.columns:
            opens[ticker] = df["open"]
        if "high" in df.columns:
            highs[ticker] = df["high"]
        if "low" in df.columns:
            lows[ticker] = df["low"]

        dt_index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
        all_dates = all_dates.union(dt_index)

    all_dates = all_dates.sort_values()

    def build_and_align(series_dict: dict, fill_method: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        if not series_dict:
            return pd.DataFrame()

        df = pd.DataFrame(series_dict)
        df = df.reindex(all_dates)

        if fill_method == "ffill":
            return df.ffill()
        elif fill_method == "zero":
            return df.fillna(0.0)
        return df

    prices_df = build_and_align(closes, fill_method="ffill")

    features = {}
    if volumes:
        features["volume"] = build_and_align(volumes, fill_method="zero")
    if opens:
        features["open"] = build_and_align(opens, fill_method="ffill")
    if highs:
        features["high"] = build_and_align(highs, fill_method="ffill")
    if lows:
        features["low"] = build_and_align(lows, fill_method="ffill")

    valid_indices = prices_df.dropna(how="all").index
    prices_df = prices_df.loc[valid_indices]

    for key in features:
        features[key] = features[key].loc[valid_indices]

    return MarketData(prices=prices_df, features=features)

docs.text:
fit(data: MarketData, log_returns: bool = False) -> None

De-Volatizes the historical time series to extract empirical shocks.

Source code in src/pyalloq-simulation/src/pyalloq_simulation/generators/fhs.py 
def fit(self, data: MarketData, log_returns: bool = False) -> None:
    """
    De-Volatizes the historical time series to extract empirical shocks.
    """
    self.data: MarketData = (
        FactorBackcastImputer().fit_transform(data) if self.impute_missing else data
    )
    self.log_returns = log_returns
    self._record_index_metadata(self.data.prices.index)
    self.initial_prices = self.data.prices.iloc[-1].to_numpy(dtype=self.dtype)
    self.std_residuals = pd.DataFrame(
        index=self.data.prices.index, columns=self.data.assets, dtype=np.float64
    )
    self.N = len(self.data.assets)
    returns = self.data.get_returns(log_returns)
    self._fit_exogenous_features(self.data, returns)

    # Suppress arch convergence warnings for cleaner SDK output
    warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning)
    scale = 100.0
    arch_dist = cast(
        Literal["normal", "t", "skewt"],
        "normal" if self.dist == "Normal" else self.dist,
    )
    for asset in self.data.assets:
        scaled_ret = returns[asset].dropna() * scale
        am = arch_model(
            scaled_ret,
            mean="Constant",
            vol="GARCH",
            p=1,
            q=1,
            dist=arch_dist,
            rescale=False,
        )

        res = am.fit(disp="off")
        params = res.params.copy()
        params["mu"] = params["mu"] / scale
        params["omega"] = params["omega"] / (scale**2)
        self.garch_params[asset] = params

        # z_t = (r_t - mu) / sigma_t (scale cancels out in ratio)
        cond_vol = pd.Series(res.conditional_volatility, index=scaled_ret.index)
        resid_s = pd.Series(res.resid, index=scaled_ret.index)
        self.std_residuals[asset] = resid_s / cond_vol
        # Store the final historical volatility state (unscaled) to seed t=0 of the simulation
        self.last_volatility[asset] = float(cond_vol.iloc[-1]) / scale

    # Drop rows with any NaNs to ensure a perfectly synchronous residual matrix
    self.std_residuals.dropna(inplace=True)
    self.is_fitted = True

generate(n_paths: int, horizon: int) -> ScenarioMarketData

Generates forward-looking synthetic paths. Args: n_paths (int): No. of Monte Carlo scenarios (M). horizon (int): Forward time steps to simulate (T).

Returns:

Name Type Description ScenarioMarketData ScenarioMarketData

A dataclass wrapping the (M, T, N) tensor.

Source code in src/pyalloq-simulation/src/pyalloq_simulation/generators/fhs.py 
def generate(self, n_paths: int, horizon: int) -> ScenarioMarketData:
    """
    Generates forward-looking synthetic paths.
    Args:
        n_paths (int): No. of Monte Carlo scenarios (M).
        horizon (int): Forward time steps to simulate (T).

    Returns:
        ScenarioMarketData: A dataclass wrapping the (M, T, N) tensor.
    """

    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError(
            "FHS needs to be fitted. Call .fit(data: MarketData) first"
        )

    T_hist = len(self.std_residuals)

    mu = np.array(
        [self.garch_params[a]["mu"] for a in self.data.assets], dtype=self.dtype
    )
    omega = np.array(
        [self.garch_params[a]["omega"] for a in self.data.assets], dtype=self.dtype
    )
    alpha = np.array(
        [self.garch_params[a]["alpha[1]"] for a in self.data.assets],
        dtype=self.dtype,
    )
    beta = np.array(
        [self.garch_params[a]["beta[1]"] for a in self.data.assets],
        dtype=self.dtype,
    )

    Z_hist = self.std_residuals.to_numpy(dtype=self.dtype)
    current_vol = np.tile(
        np.array(
            [self.last_volatility[a] for a in self.data.assets], dtype=self.dtype
        ),
        (n_paths, 1),
    )
    synthetic_returns = np.zeros((n_paths, horizon, self.N), dtype=self.dtype)
    random_indices = np.random.randint(0, T_hist, size=(n_paths, horizon))

    for t in range(horizon):
        idx = random_indices[:, t]
        Z_t = Z_hist[idx, :]
        sim_returns = mu + (current_vol * Z_t)
        synthetic_returns[:, t, :] = sim_returns
        current_var = (
            omega + alpha * (current_vol * Z_t) ** 2 + beta * (current_vol**2)
        )
        current_vol = np.sqrt(np.maximum(current_var, 1e-12)).astype(
            self.dtype, copy=False
        )

    if self.log_returns:
        synthetic_prices = self.initial_prices * np.exp(
            np.cumsum(synthetic_returns, axis=1)
        )
    else:
        synthetic_prices = self.initial_prices * np.cumprod(
            1.0 + synthetic_returns, axis=1
        )

    synthetic_prices = synthetic_prices.astype(self.dtype, copy=False)
    sim_features, feat_cols = self._simulate_exogenous_features(synthetic_returns)

    return ScenarioMarketData(
        prices=synthetic_prices,
        returns=synthetic_returns,
        asset_names=list(self.data.assets),
        initial_prices=self.initial_prices.copy(),
        timestamps=self._build_future_timestamps(horizon),
        features=sim_features,
        feature_columns=feat_cols,
    )

GARCH-EVT-Student-t Copula Monte Carlo Generator.

  1. Filters univariate marginals via AR(1)-GARCH(1,1) to extract i.i.d. standardized residuals.
  2. Models marginal tails with Extreme Value Theory (Peaks-Over-Threshold Generalized Pareto Distribution) and the interior with the empirical distribution.
  3. Binds marginals via a Student-t Copula with correlation matrix R and degrees of freedom nu to capture asymmetric tail risk and lower-tail dependence (lambda_L > 0).
Source code in src/pyalloq-simulation/src/pyalloq_simulation/generators/copulas.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    nu: float = 5.0,
    lower_quantile: float = 0.10,
    upper_quantile: float = 0.90,
    mean_model: str = "AR",
    dtype: Any = np.float32,
    impute_missing: bool = True,
) -> None:
    if nu <= 2.0:
        raise ValueError("Student-t degrees of freedom `nu` must be > 2.0.")
    if not (0.01 <= lower_quantile < upper_quantile <= 0.99):
        raise ValueError(
            "Quantile thresholds must satisfy 0.01 <= lower_quantile < upper_quantile <= 0.99."
        )
    self.nu = float(nu)
    self.q_lower = float(lower_quantile)
    self.q_upper = float(upper_quantile)
    self.mean_model = mean_model
    self.dtype = np.dtype(dtype)
    self.impute_missing = impute_missing

    self.is_fitted = False

    Decodes real-time posterior regime probabilities p_k(t) on a MarketData instance.
    """
    if not self.is_fitted or self.gmm is None or self.regime_order is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "GMMRegimeGenerator needs to be fitted. Call .fit() first."
        )
    clean_data = (
        FactorBackcastImputer().fit_transform(data) if self.impute_missing else data
    )
    returns = clean_data.get_returns(self.log_returns)
    ret_np = returns.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    probs = self.gmm.predict_proba(ret_np)[:, self.regime_order]
    return pd.DataFrame(probs, index=returns.index, columns=self.regime_labels)

def build(
    self, views: list[ViewType]
) -> tuple[
    np.ndarray | None, np.ndarray | None, np.ndarray | None, np.ndarray | None
]:
    """
    Parses views and returns (A_ineq, b_ineq, C_eq, d_eq).
    Returns None for matrices if no corresponding constraints exist.
    """
    A_ineq: list[np.ndarray] = []
    b_ineq: list[float] = []
    C_eq: list[np.ndarray] = []
    d_eq: list[float] = []

    # Track reference means and volatilities for centering second-moment views
    ref_means: dict[str, float] = {
        name: float(np.mean(self._get_asset_vector(name)))
        for name in self.asset_names
    }
    ref_stds: dict[str, float] = {
        name: float(np.std(self._get_asset_vector(name)))
        for name in self.asset_names
    }

    for view in views:
        if isinstance(view, AbsoluteView) and view.operator == "==":
            if view.asset in self.asset_idx:
                ref_means[view.asset] = float(view.target)

    for view in views:
        if isinstance(view, VolatilityView):
            vec = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset)
            prior_std = float(np.std(vec))
            target_vol = (
                float(view.target_volatility)
                if view.target_volatility is not None
                else prior_std * float(view.multiplier)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            )
            ref_stds[view.asset] = target_vol

    for view in views:
        if isinstance(view, AbsoluteView):
            condition_vector = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset)
            target_val = float(view.target)
        elif isinstance(view, RelativeView):
            vec_out = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset_outperformer)
            vec_under = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset_underperformer)
            condition_vector = vec_out - vec_under
            target_val = float(view.target)
        elif isinstance(view, VolatilityView):
            vec = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset)
            mean_val = ref_means[view.asset]
            prior_std = float(np.std(vec))
            target_vol = (
                float(view.target_volatility)
                if view.target_volatility is not None
                else prior_std * float(view.multiplier)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            )
            condition_vector = (vec - mean_val) ** 2
            target_val = target_vol**2
        elif isinstance(view, CovarianceView):
            vec1 = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset_1)
            vec2 = self._get_asset_vector(view.asset_2)
            m1 = ref_means[view.asset_1]
            m2 = ref_means[view.asset_2]
            condition_vector = (vec1 - m1) * (vec2 - m2)
            if view.target_covariance is not None:
                target_val = float(view.target_covariance)
            else:
                target_val = (
                    float(view.target_correlation)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                    * ref_stds[view.asset_1]
                    * ref_stds[view.asset_2]
                )
        else:
            raise TypeError("Unsupported view type.")

        if view.operator == "==":
            C_eq.append(condition_vector)
            d_eq.append(target_val)
        elif view.operator == "<=":
            A_ineq.append(condition_vector)
            b_ineq.append(target_val)
        elif view.operator == ">=":
            A_ineq.append(-condition_vector)
            b_ineq.append(-target_val)

    A_out = np.vstack(A_ineq) if A_ineq else None
    b_out = np.array(b_ineq, dtype=np.float64) if b_ineq else None
    C_out = np.vstack(C_eq) if C_eq else None
    d_out = np.array(d_eq, dtype=np.float64) if d_eq else None

    return A_out, b_out, C_out, d_out

def fit(
    self,
    A_ineq: np.ndarray | None = None,
    b_ineq: np.ndarray | None = None,
    C_eq: np.ndarray | None = None,
    d_eq: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> EntropyResult:
    """
    Calculates posterior probability distribution over scenarios.

    Args:
        A_ineq: Shape (K_ineq, M) such that A_ineq @ x <= b_ineq
        b_ineq: Shape (K_ineq,)
        C_eq:   Shape (K_eq, M) such that C_eq @ x == d_eq
        d_eq:   Shape (K_eq,)
    """
    # Determine number of constraints
    k_ineq = len(b_ineq) if b_ineq is not None else 0
    k_eq = len(d_eq) if d_eq is not None else 0
    total_views = k_ineq + k_eq

    if total_views == 0:
        return EntropyResult(
            weights=self.p.copy(),
            prior=self.p.copy(),
            kl_divergence=0.0,
            success=True,
            message="No views supplied; returned prior.",
        )

    # Standardize constraints: stack into joint matrix G = [C; A]
    matrices: list[np.ndarray] = []
    bounds_targets: list[np.ndarray] = []

    if k_eq > 0 and C_eq is not None and d_eq is not None:
        matrices.append(C_eq)
        bounds_targets.append(d_eq)
    if k_ineq > 0 and A_ineq is not None and b_ineq is not None:
        matrices.append(A_ineq)
        bounds_targets.append(b_ineq)

    G = np.vstack(matrices)  # Shape: (V, M)
    targets: np.ndarray = np.concatenate(bounds_targets)  # Shape: (V,)

    # Dual bounds: lambda (equality) is unconstrained (-inf, inf),
    # nu (inequality) is constrained to [0, inf)
    bounds = [(None, None)] * k_eq + [(0.0, None)] * k_ineq
    init_dual = np.zeros(total_views)

    # Dual objective and analytical gradient
    def dual_objective(gamma):
        # gamma is [lambda, nu], shape: (V,)
        # exponent shape: (M,)
        exponent = -np.dot(gamma, G)

        # Log-sum-exp trick to prevent numerical overflow
        max_exp = np.max(exponent)
        weights_unnorm = self.p * np.exp(exponent - max_exp)
        partition_fn = np.sum(weights_unnorm)

        # Dual function value
        dual_val = np.log(partition_fn) + max_exp + np.dot(gamma, targets)

        # Analytical gradient w.r.t gamma: targets - (G @ posterior_probabilities)
        prob = weights_unnorm / partition_fn
        grad = targets - np.dot(G, prob)

        return dual_val, grad

    # Optimize dual problem using L-BFGS-B
    opt_res = minimize(
        fun=dual_objective,
        x0=init_dual,
        method="L-BFGS-B",
        jac=True,
        bounds=bounds,
        options={"ftol": 1e-12, "gtol": 1e-10, "maxiter": 500},
    )

    # Recover posterior probabilities x* algebraically
    optimal_gamma = opt_res.x
    exponent = -np.dot(optimal_gamma, G)
    max_exp = np.max(exponent)
    unnorm_x = self.p * np.exp(exponent - max_exp)
    x_post = unnorm_x / np.sum(unnorm_x)

    kl = np.sum(np.where(x_post > 1e-16, x_post * np.log(x_post / self.p), 0.0))

    return EntropyResult(
        weights=x_post,
        prior=self.p,
        kl_divergence=kl,
        success=opt_res.success,
        message=opt_res.message,
    )

Calculates probability-weighted terminal and path-dependent portfolio metrics across the simulation horizon T.

Source code in src/pyalloq-simulation/src/pyalloq_simulation/core/evaluator.py 
def evaluate(
    self,
    scenario_data: ScenarioMarketData,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray,
    entropy_result: EntropyResult,
    ruin_threshold: float | None = None,
) -> EvaluationMetrics:
    """
    Calculates probability-weighted terminal and path-dependent portfolio metrics
    across the simulation horizon T.
    """
    weights = np.asarray(asset_weights, dtype=np.float64)
    probs = np.asarray(entropy_result.weights, dtype=np.float64)  # Shape: (M,)

    cumulative_asset_returns = scenario_data.get_cumulative_returns().astype(
        np.float64
    )  # Shape: (M, N)
    portfolio_returns = np.dot(cumulative_asset_returns, weights)

    expected_return = float(np.dot(portfolio_returns, probs))

    variance = float(np.dot(probs, (portfolio_returns - expected_return) ** 2))
    volatility = float(np.sqrt(max(variance, 0.0)))
    sharpe = (expected_return - self.rf) / volatility if volatility > 0 else 0.0

    sort_idx = np.argsort(portfolio_returns)
    sorted_rets = portfolio_returns[sort_idx]
    sorted_probs = probs[sort_idx]

    cum_probs = np.cumsum(sorted_probs)
    alpha = 0.05
    tail_idx = np.where(cum_probs <= alpha)[0]

    if len(tail_idx) == 0:
        # Fallback if the very first scenario carries > 5% probability mass
        cvar_95 = float(sorted_rets[0])
    else:
        # Normalize the tail probabilities so they sum to 1.0
        tail_probs = sorted_probs[tail_idx] / np.sum(sorted_probs[tail_idx])
        cvar_95 = float(np.dot(sorted_rets[tail_idx], tail_probs))

    # Path-dependent intra-horizon metrics along axis=1 (time steps 0..T)
    M = scenario_data.prices.shape[0]
    if scenario_data.initial_prices is not None:
        init_p = np.asarray(scenario_data.initial_prices, dtype=np.float64)[
            None, None, :
        ]
        rel_prices = scenario_data.prices.astype(np.float64) / init_p
        # Portfolio wealth at each step t=1..T: (M, T)
        step_wealth: np.ndarray = np.tensordot(rel_prices, weights, axes=([2], [0]))
    else:
        step_port_rets = np.tensordot(
            scenario_data.returns.astype(np.float64), weights, axes=([2], [0])
        )
        step_wealth = np.cumprod(1.0 + step_port_rets, axis=1).astype(np.float64)

    # Prepend t=0 initial portfolio equity = 1.0 -> shape (M, T + 1)
    wealth_curve = np.concatenate(
        [np.ones((M, 1), dtype=np.float64), step_wealth], axis=1
    )
    running_peaks = np.maximum.accumulate(wealth_curve, axis=1)
    drawdowns = (wealth_curve - running_peaks) / np.maximum(running_peaks, 1e-12)
    path_mdds = np.min(drawdowns, axis=1)  # Shape: (M,), values <= 0.0

    view_adjusted_mdd = float(np.dot(probs, path_mdds))

    eff_threshold = (
        -abs(ruin_threshold) if ruin_threshold is not None else self.ruin_threshold
    )
    # Ruin occurs if intra-horizon drawdown or equity drop breaches threshold
    min_equity_return = np.min(wealth_curve - 1.0, axis=1)
    ruin_mask = (path_mdds <= eff_threshold) | (min_equity_return <= eff_threshold)
    probability_of_ruin = float(np.dot(probs, ruin_mask.astype(np.float64)))

    return EvaluationMetrics(
        expected_return=expected_return,
        volatility=volatility,
        sharpe_ratio=sharpe,
        cvar_95=cvar_95,
        view_adjusted_mdd=view_adjusted_mdd,
        probability_of_ruin=probability_of_ruin,
    )

def __init__(
    self,
    backtest_or_pbo: BacktestResult
    | PBOResult
    | pd.DataFrame
    | np.ndarray
    | Sequence[BacktestResult],
    cpcv_or_synthetic: CPCVResult | MonteCarloResult | None = None,
    n_groups: int = 6,
    n_partitions: int = 8,
) -> None:
    self.n_groups = n_groups
    self.n_partitions = n_partitions

    # Resolve CPCVResult
    if isinstance(cpcv_or_synthetic, CPCVResult):
        self.cpcv_result = cpcv_or_synthetic
    elif isinstance(backtest_or_pbo, BacktestResult):
        self.cpcv_result = CPCVSplitter(n_groups=n_groups).scramble_timelines(
            backtest_or_pbo
        )
    elif isinstance(backtest_or_pbo, pd.DataFrame):
        # Use first column or mean strategy for CPCV scrambling
        self.cpcv_result = CPCVSplitter(n_groups=n_groups).scramble_timelines(
            backtest_or_pbo.iloc[:, 0]
        )
    elif (
        isinstance(backtest_or_pbo, Sequence)
        and len(backtest_or_pbo) > 0
        and isinstance(backtest_or_pbo[0], BacktestResult)
    ):
        self.cpcv_result = CPCVSplitter(n_groups=n_groups).scramble_timelines(
            backtest_or_pbo[0]
        )
    else:
        arr = np.asarray(backtest_or_pbo, dtype=np.float64)
        col0 = arr[:, 0] if arr.ndim == 2 else arr
        self.cpcv_result = CPCVSplitter(n_groups=n_groups).scramble_timelines(
            pd.Series(col0)
        )

    # Resolve PBOResult
    evaluator = PBOEvaluator(n_partitions=n_partitions)
    if isinstance(backtest_or_pbo, PBOResult):
        self.pbo_result = backtest_or_pbo
    elif isinstance(backtest_or_pbo, BacktestResult):
        comp = (
            cpcv_or_synthetic if cpcv_or_synthetic is not None else self.cpcv_result
        )
        self.pbo_result = evaluator.evaluate_benchmark(backtest_or_pbo, comp)
    else:
        self.pbo_result = evaluator.evaluate_cscv(backtest_or_pbo)

def plot_fan_chart(
    source: MonteCarloResult | ScenarioMarketData | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    entropy_result: EntropyResult | None = None,
    percentiles: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] = (
        (5.0, 95.0),
        (10.0, 90.0),
        (25.0, 75.0),
    ),
    benchmark: BacktestResult | pd.Series | None = None,
    n_sample_paths: int = 15,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Probabilistic Equity Cone (Fan Chart)",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Plots the median equity trajectory enveloped by shaded confidence intervals
    (e.g., 5th-95th, 10th-90th, 25th-75th percentiles) across synthetic futures.
    Supports probability-weighted quantiles when `entropy_result` is provided.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    equity_paths, timestamps = extract_equity_paths(source, asset_weights=asset_weights)
    M, T = equity_paths.shape
    x_vals = list(timestamps)

    probs = (
        np.asarray(entropy_result.weights, dtype=np.float64)
        if entropy_result is not None
        else None
    )

    fig = go.Figure()

    # Optional faint sample spaghetti trajectories
    if n_sample_paths > 0 and M > 0:
        n_draw = min(n_sample_paths, M)
        sample_indices = np.linspace(0, M - 1, n_draw, dtype=int)
        for idx in sample_indices:
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=x_vals,
                    y=equity_paths[idx],
                    mode="lines",
                    line={"color": hex_to_rgba(palette.slate, 0.16), "width": 1},
                    hoverinfo="skip",
                    showlegend=False,
                    name=f"Path {idx}",
                )
            )

    # Sort percentile bands from widest to narrowest
    sorted_bands = sorted(percentiles, key=lambda b: b[1] - b[0], reverse=True)
    alphas = np.linspace(0.14, 0.32, max(1, len(sorted_bands)))

    for (low_p, high_p), alpha_val in zip(sorted_bands, alphas):
        q_pair = weighted_quantiles(
            equity_paths, [low_p / 100.0, high_p / 100.0], sample_weight=probs
        )
        q_low, q_high = q_pair[0], q_pair[1]

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=q_high,
                mode="lines",
                line={"width": 0},
                hoverinfo="skip",
                showlegend=False,
                name=f"{high_p:.0f}th Percentile",
            )
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=q_low,
                mode="lines",
                line={"width": 0},
                fill="tonexty",
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.emerald, float(alpha_val)),
                name=f"{low_p:.0f}th–{high_p:.0f}th Percentile Band",
                hovertemplate=f"{low_p:.0f}th–{high_p:.0f}th Band: %{{y:.3f}}<extra></extra>",
            )
        )

    # Median & Mean trajectories
    median_curve = weighted_quantiles(equity_paths, [0.50], sample_weight=probs)[0]
    mean_curve = (
        np.average(equity_paths, axis=0, weights=probs)
        if probs is not None
        else np.mean(equity_paths, axis=0)
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=median_curve,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 3},
            name="Median Trajectory (50th Pct)",
            hovertemplate="Median Wealth: %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=mean_curve,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.cyan, "width": 2, "dash": "dash"},
            name="Expected (Mean) Trajectory",
            hovertemplate="Expected Wealth: %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

    if benchmark is not None:
        bench_eq = (
            benchmark.equity_curve
            if isinstance(benchmark, BacktestResult)
            else pd.Series(benchmark)
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=list(bench_eq.index),
                y=bench_eq.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.amber, "width": 2.2},
                name="Realized / Benchmark Equity",
            )
        )

    # Initial wealth reference line
    fig.add_hline(
        y=1.0,
        line_dash="dot",
        line_color=palette.border_color,
        annotation_text="Initial Capital (1.0)",
        annotation_position="bottom right",
    )

    subtitle = f"Dispersion across {M:,} synthetic paths over {T} horizon steps"
    if entropy_result is not None:
        subtitle += f" (View-Adjusted Posterior, KL={entropy_result.kl_divergence:.4f})"

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Simulation Horizon / Date")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Portfolio Equity (Normalized = 1.0)")
    return fig

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/simulation.py 
def plot_terminal_wealth_ruin(
    source: MonteCarloResult | ScenarioMarketData | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    entropy_result: EntropyResult | None = None,
    ruin_threshold: float = -0.20,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Terminal Wealth Distribution & Probability of Ruin",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Plots the density distribution of the portfolio's terminal wealth, isolating
    the probability mass falling below the ruin threshold (1 + ruin_threshold).
    Also reports path-dependent intra-horizon ruin probability.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    equity_paths, _ = extract_equity_paths(source, asset_weights=asset_weights)
    M, _ = equity_paths.shape
    terminal_wealth = equity_paths[:, -1]

    probs = (
        np.asarray(entropy_result.weights, dtype=np.float64)
        if entropy_result is not None
        else np.full(M, 1.0 / M, dtype=np.float64)
    )
    probs = probs / np.sum(probs)

    # Normalize ruin_threshold: if negative (e.g. -0.20), terminal ruin wealth is 1.0 - 0.20 = 0.80
    ruin_drop = -abs(ruin_threshold)
    wealth_ruin_level = 1.0 + ruin_drop

    # Terminal ruin probability & path-dependent intra-horizon ruin probability
    terminal_ruin_mask = terminal_wealth <= wealth_ruin_level
    prob_terminal_ruin = float(np.dot(probs, terminal_ruin_mask.astype(np.float64)))

    drawdowns = compute_drawdown_paths(equity_paths)
    path_mdds = np.min(drawdowns, axis=1)
    min_wealth = np.min(equity_paths, axis=1)
    intra_ruin_mask = (path_mdds <= ruin_drop) | (min_wealth <= wealth_ruin_level)
    prob_path_ruin = float(np.dot(probs, intra_ruin_mask.astype(np.float64)))

    expected_wealth = float(np.dot(probs, terminal_wealth))

    x_kde, y_kde = compute_kde_1d(terminal_wealth, weights=probs, n_points=300)

    fig = go.Figure()

    # Histogram of terminal wealth
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Histogram(
            x=terminal_wealth,
            histnorm="probability density",
            nbinsx=min(50, max(15, M // 8)),
            marker={
                "color": hex_to_rgba(palette.teal, 0.35),
                "line": {"color": hex_to_rgba(palette.teal, 0.7), "width": 1},
            },
            name="Terminal Wealth Histogram",
            hovertemplate="Terminal Wealth: %{x:.3f}<br>Density: %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

    # Full KDE curve
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_kde,
            y=y_kde,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 2.5},
            name="Wealth Density (KDE)",
        )
    )

    # Shaded ruin tail (x <= wealth_ruin_level)
    ruin_x = x_kde[x_kde <= wealth_ruin_level]
    ruin_y = y_kde[x_kde <= wealth_ruin_level]
    if len(ruin_x) > 1:
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=ruin_x,
                y=ruin_y,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.crimson, "width": 2},
                fill="tozeroy",
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.crimson, 0.45),
                name=f"Ruin Tail (≤ {wealth_ruin_level:.2f})",
            )
        )

    # Vertical threshold lines
    fig.add_vline(
        x=wealth_ruin_level,
        line_dash="dash",
        line_color=palette.crimson,
        line_width=2.5,
        annotation_text=f"Ruin Threshold ({wealth_ruin_level:.2f}) | Terminal Ruin: {prob_terminal_ruin:.1%}",
        annotation_position="top left",
        annotation_font_color=palette.crimson,
    )
    fig.add_vline(
        x=expected_wealth,
        line_dash="dot",
        line_color=palette.cyan,
        line_width=2,
        annotation_text=f"E[W_T] = {expected_wealth:.3f}",
        annotation_position="top right",
        annotation_font_color=palette.cyan,
    )

    subtitle = (
        f"Terminal Ruin Prob: {prob_terminal_ruin:.2%} | "
        f"Intra-Horizon Ruin Prob (DD ≤ {ruin_drop:.0%}): {prob_path_ruin:.2%} | "
        f"Expected Terminal Wealth: {expected_wealth:.3f}"
    )
    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Terminal Portfolio Wealth (W_T)")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Probability Density")
    return fig

def plot_cvar_tail_risk(
    source: MonteCarloResult
    | ScenarioMarketData
    | BacktestResult
    | pd.DataFrame
    | pd.Series
    | np.ndarray,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    entropy_result: EntropyResult | None = None,
    alpha: float = 0.05,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Return Distribution & CVaR Tail-Risk Shading",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    On the return distribution histogram, visually isolates the left tail to demonstrate
    Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR / Expected Shortfall) during
    extreme market crashes.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    if isinstance(source, BacktestResult):
        returns_1d = source.returns.dropna().to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        probs = np.full(len(returns_1d), 1.0 / max(1, len(returns_1d)))
        horizon_label = "Daily / Period Portfolio Return"
    elif isinstance(source, pd.Series):
        returns_1d = source.dropna().to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        probs = np.full(len(returns_1d), 1.0 / max(1, len(returns_1d)))
        horizon_label = "Portfolio Return"
    elif isinstance(source, np.ndarray) and source.ndim == 1:
        returns_1d = source.astype(np.float64)
        probs = np.full(len(returns_1d), 1.0 / max(1, len(returns_1d)))
        horizon_label = "Portfolio Return"
    else:
        equity_paths, _ = extract_equity_paths(source, asset_weights=asset_weights)
        returns_1d = equity_paths[:, -1] - 1.0
        probs = (
            np.asarray(entropy_result.weights, dtype=np.float64)
            if entropy_result is not None
            else np.full(len(returns_1d), 1.0 / max(1, len(returns_1d)))
        )
        horizon_label = "Cumulative Horizon Return"

    probs = probs / np.sum(probs)

    # Calculate probability-weighted VaR and CVaR
    sort_idx = np.argsort(returns_1d)
    sorted_rets = returns_1d[sort_idx]
    sorted_probs = probs[sort_idx]
    cum_probs = np.cumsum(sorted_probs)

    var_alpha = float(weighted_quantiles(returns_1d, [alpha], sample_weight=probs)[0])
    tail_idx = np.where(cum_probs <= alpha)[0]
    if len(tail_idx) == 0:
        cvar_alpha = float(sorted_rets[0])
    else:
        tail_p = sorted_probs[tail_idx] / np.sum(sorted_probs[tail_idx])
        cvar_alpha = float(np.dot(sorted_rets[tail_idx], tail_p))

    mean_ret = float(np.dot(returns_1d, probs))
    conf_pct = round((1.0 - alpha) * 100)

    x_kde, y_kde = compute_kde_1d(returns_1d, weights=probs, n_points=300)

    fig = go.Figure()

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Histogram(
            x=returns_1d,
            histnorm="probability density",
            nbinsx=min(55, max(15, len(returns_1d) // 8)),
            marker={
                "color": hex_to_rgba(palette.slate, 0.35),
                "line": {"color": hex_to_rgba(palette.slate, 0.65), "width": 1},
            },
            name="Return Distribution",
        )
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_kde,
            y=y_kde,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.cyan, "width": 2.5},
            name="Return Density (KDE)",
        )
    )

    # Shade the left tail <= VaR_alpha
    tail_x = x_kde[x_kde <= var_alpha]
    tail_y = y_kde[x_kde <= var_alpha]
    if len(tail_x) == 0:
        tail_x = np.array([np.min(x_kde), var_alpha])
        tail_y = np.interp(tail_x, x_kde, y_kde)

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=tail_x,
            y=tail_y,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.coral, "width": 2},
            fill="tozeroy",
            fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.coral, 0.45),
            name=f"{conf_pct}% Tail Shortfall Region (≤ VaR)",
        )
    )

    fig.add_vline(
        x=var_alpha,
        line_dash="dash",
        line_color=palette.amber,
        line_width=2,
        annotation_text=f"VaR {conf_pct}%: {var_alpha:.2%}",
        annotation_position="top right",
        annotation_font_color=palette.amber,
    )
    fig.add_vline(
        x=cvar_alpha,
        line_dash="solid",
        line_color=palette.crimson,
        line_width=2.8,
        annotation_text=f"CVaR {conf_pct}% (Expected Shortfall): {cvar_alpha:.2%}",
        annotation_position="top left",
        annotation_font_color=palette.crimson,
    )

    subtitle = (
        f"Mean Return: {mean_ret:.2%} | "
        f"VaR ({conf_pct}%): {var_alpha:.2%} | "
        f"CVaR ({conf_pct}%): {cvar_alpha:.2%}"
    )
    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text=horizon_label, tickformat=".1%")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Probability Density")
    return fig

def plot_drawdown_fan_chart(
    source: MonteCarloResult | ScenarioMarketData | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    entropy_result: EntropyResult | None = None,
    percentiles: Sequence[tuple[float, float]] = (
        (5.0, 95.0),
        (10.0, 90.0),
        (25.0, 75.0),
    ),
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Underwater Drawdown Fan Chart",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Plots an underwater area chart of the probability distribution of drawdowns across
    all synthetic paths, illustrating loss severity and duration across the multiverse.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    equity_paths, timestamps = extract_equity_paths(source, asset_weights=asset_weights)
    drawdown_paths = compute_drawdown_paths(equity_paths)
    x_vals = list(timestamps)

    probs = (
        np.asarray(entropy_result.weights, dtype=np.float64)
        if entropy_result is not None
        else None
    )

    fig = go.Figure()

    sorted_bands = sorted(percentiles, key=lambda b: b[1] - b[0], reverse=True)
    alphas = np.linspace(0.14, 0.34, max(1, len(sorted_bands)))

    for (low_p, high_p), alpha_val in zip(sorted_bands, alphas):
        q_pair = weighted_quantiles(
            drawdown_paths, [low_p / 100.0, high_p / 100.0], sample_weight=probs
        )
        q_worst, q_mild = q_pair[0], q_pair[1]

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=q_mild,
                mode="lines",
                line={"width": 0},
                hoverinfo="skip",
                showlegend=False,
            )
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=q_worst,
                mode="lines",
                line={"width": 0},
                fill="tonexty",
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.coral, float(alpha_val)),
                name=f"{low_p:.0f}th–{high_p:.0f}th Drawdown Band",
                hovertemplate=f"{low_p:.0f}th–{high_p:.0f}th DD: %{{y:.2%}}<extra></extra>",
            )
        )

    median_dd = weighted_quantiles(drawdown_paths, [0.50], sample_weight=probs)[0]
    worst_5pct_dd = weighted_quantiles(drawdown_paths, [0.05], sample_weight=probs)[0]

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=median_dd,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.coral, "width": 2.8},
            name="Median Drawdown (50th Pct)",
            hovertemplate="Median Drawdown: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=worst_5pct_dd,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.crimson, "width": 2, "dash": "dash"},
            name="Tail Drawdown (5th Pct)",
            hovertemplate="5th Pct Drawdown: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

    path_mdds = np.min(drawdown_paths, axis=1)
    expected_mdd = (
        float(np.dot(probs / np.sum(probs), path_mdds))
        if probs is not None
        else float(np.mean(path_mdds))
    )

    fig.add_hline(y=0.0, line_color=palette.border_color, line_width=1.5)

    subtitle = (
        f"Expected Max Drawdown across paths: {expected_mdd:.2%} | "
        f"95th Percentile Worst Drawdown: {float(np.min(worst_5pct_dd)):.2%}"
    )
    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Simulation Horizon / Date")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Underwater Drawdown (%)", tickformat=".1%")
    return fig

Right panel plots In-Sample vs Out-of-Sample Sharpe Ratios with OLS degradation slope. - In Single-Strategy Benchmark mode (when synthetic_comparison is provided or PBOResult.mode == 'benchmark'): Left panel plots the simulated/scrambled Sharpe ratio distribution against the strategy's historical backtest Sharpe ratio. def plot_pbo_distribution(
    pbo_source: PBOResult | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray | Sequence[BacktestResult],
    synthetic_comparison: MonteCarloResult
    | CPCVResult
    | pd.Series
    | np.ndarray
    | None = None,
    n_partitions: int = 8,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO) & Performance Degradation",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Visualizes the Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO):
    - In CSCV mode (or when given a PBOResult from CSCV / a (T, M) strategy matrix):
      Left panel plots the distribution of Rank Logits (lambda) with shaded overfitting mass (lambda <= 0).
      Right panel plots In-Sample vs Out-of-Sample Sharpe Ratios with OLS degradation slope.
    - In Single-Strategy Benchmark mode (when `synthetic_comparison` is provided or `PBOResult.mode == 'benchmark'`):
      Left panel plots the simulated/scrambled Sharpe ratio distribution against the strategy's
      historical backtest Sharpe ratio.
      Right panel plots the Empirical Cumulative Distribution (ECDF) and survival probability.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    if isinstance(pbo_source, PBOResult):
        res = pbo_source
    elif synthetic_comparison is not None:
        evaluator = PBOEvaluator(n_partitions=n_partitions)
        if isinstance(pbo_source, (BacktestResult, pd.Series, float, int)):
            res = evaluator.evaluate_benchmark(pbo_source, synthetic_comparison)
        else:
            res = evaluator.evaluate_cscv(pbo_source)
    else:
        evaluator = PBOEvaluator(n_partitions=n_partitions)
        res = evaluator.evaluate_cscv(pbo_source)

    if res.mode == "cscv":
        fig = make_subplots(
            rows=1,
            cols=2,
            subplot_titles=(
                f"Rank Logit (λ) Distribution — PBO = {res.pbo:.1%}",
                f"IS vs. OOS Sharpe Degradation (P[SR_OOS < 0] = {res.prob_oos_loss:.1%})",
            ),
            horizontal_spacing=0.10,
        )

        logits = res.logits
        x_kde, y_kde = compute_kde_1d(logits, n_points=250)

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Histogram(
                x=logits,
                histnorm="probability density",
                nbinsx=min(35, max(10, len(logits) // 3)),
                marker={
                    "color": hex_to_rgba(palette.slate, 0.35),
                    "line": {"color": hex_to_rgba(palette.slate, 0.7), "width": 1},
                },
                name="Logit Histogram",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_kde,
                y=y_kde,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.cyan, "width": 2.5},
                name="Logit Density (KDE)",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

        # Overfit region: lambda <= 0
        overfit_x = x_kde[x_kde <= 0.0]
        overfit_y = y_kde[x_kde <= 0.0]
        if len(overfit_x) > 1:
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=overfit_x,
                    y=overfit_y,
                    mode="lines",
                    line={"color": palette.crimson, "width": 2},
                    fill="tozeroy",
                    fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.crimson, 0.42),
                    name=f"Overfit Mass (λ ≤ 0): {res.pbo:.1%}",
                ),
                row=1,
                col=1,
            )

        fig.add_vline(
            x=0.0,
            line_dash="dash",
            line_color=palette.crimson,
            line_width=2,
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

        # Panel 2: IS vs OOS Sharpe scatter + regression line
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=res.is_sharpes,
                y=res.oos_sharpes,
                mode="markers",
                marker={
                    "size": 8,
                    "color": np.where(
                        res.oos_sharpes >= 0.0, palette.emerald, palette.coral
                    ),
                    "opacity": 0.8,
                    "line": {"width": 0.5, "color": palette.bg_primary},
                },
                name="CSCV Split (IS vs OOS SR)",
                hovertemplate="IS Sharpe: %{x:.2f}<br>OOS Sharpe: %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )

        x_line = np.linspace(
            float(np.min(res.is_sharpes)), float(np.max(res.is_sharpes)), 50
        )
        y_line = res.degradation_slope * x_line + res.degradation_intercept
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_line,
                y=y_line,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.amber, "width": 2.2, "dash": "dash"},
                name=f"Degradation Fit (Slope={res.degradation_slope:.2f})",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_hline(
            y=0.0, line_dash="dot", line_color=palette.border_color, row=1, col=2
        )

        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Rank Logit (λ_c)", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Density", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="In-Sample Sharpe Ratio (SR_IS)", row=1, col=2)
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Out-of-Sample Sharpe Ratio (SR_OOS)", row=1, col=2)
        subtitle = (
            f"CSCV Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO): {res.pbo:.1%} | "
            f"Prob. of OOS Loss: {res.prob_oos_loss:.1%} | "
            f"Degradation Slope: {res.degradation_slope:.2f}"
        )

    else:
        # Benchmark / Single-Strategy vs Synthetic/CPCV Sharpe distribution
        sim_srs = res.oos_sharpes
        hist_sr = res.historical_sharpe if res.historical_sharpe is not None else 0.0
        pct_rank = float(np.mean(sim_srs <= hist_sr))

        fig = make_subplots(
            rows=1,
            cols=2,
            subplot_titles=(
                "Simulated / Scrambled Sharpe vs. Historical Backtest",
                "Empirical CDF & Strategy Survival Probability",
            ),
            horizontal_spacing=0.10,
        )

        x_kde, y_kde = compute_kde_1d(sim_srs, n_points=250)

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Histogram(
                x=sim_srs,
                histnorm="probability density",
                nbinsx=min(40, max(12, len(sim_srs) // 5)),
                marker={
                    "color": hex_to_rgba(palette.teal, 0.35),
                    "line": {"color": hex_to_rgba(palette.teal, 0.7), "width": 1},
                },
                name="Simulated Sharpe Distribution",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_kde,
                y=y_kde,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 2.5},
                name="Sharpe Density (KDE)",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

        # Shade region where Sharpe < 0
        neg_x = x_kde[x_kde <= 0.0]
        neg_y = y_kde[x_kde <= 0.0]
        if len(neg_x) > 1:
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=neg_x,
                    y=neg_y,
                    mode="lines",
                    line={"color": palette.crimson, "width": 2},
                    fill="tozeroy",
                    fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.crimson, 0.4),
                    name=f"Negative Sharpe Mass ({res.prob_oos_loss:.1%})",
                ),
                row=1,
                col=1,
            )

        fig.add_vline(
            x=hist_sr,
            line_dash="solid",
            line_color=palette.amber,
            line_width=3,
            annotation_text=f"Historical SR: {hist_sr:.2f} ({pct_rank:.0%} pct)",
            annotation_position="top right",
            annotation_font_color=palette.amber,
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

        # Panel 2: Empirical CDF
        sorted_sr = np.sort(sim_srs)
        ecdf_y = np.arange(1, len(sorted_sr) + 1) / len(sorted_sr)
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=sorted_sr,
                y=ecdf_y,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.cyan, "width": 2.5},
                name="Simulated Sharpe ECDF",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_vline(
            x=hist_sr,
            line_dash="dash",
            line_color=palette.amber,
            line_width=2,
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_hline(
            y=pct_rank,
            line_dash="dot",
            line_color=palette.amber,
            line_width=1.5,
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )

        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Annualized Sharpe Ratio", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Density", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Annualized Sharpe Ratio", row=1, col=2)
        fig.update_yaxes(
            title_text="Cumulative Probability", tickformat=".0%", row=1, col=2
        )
        subtitle = (
            f"Historical Backtest Sharpe: {hist_sr:.2f} (Percentile: {pct_rank:.1%}) | "
            f"Simulated Mean Sharpe: {float(np.mean(sim_srs)):.2f} | "
            f"Prob(Sharpe < 0): {res.prob_oos_loss:.1%}"
        )

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=500)
    return fig

def plot_cpcv_paths(
    cpcv_source: CPCVResult | BacktestResult | pd.Series,
    n_groups: int = 6,
    max_paths_display: int = 50,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Combinatorial Scrambling (CPCV) Timeline Survival",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Visualizes strategy survival when historical data blocks are recombined into
    combinatorial timelines, scrambling the chronological order of market regimes.
    Left panel: Combinatorial equity trajectories + median/quantile envelope vs. original historical path.
    Right panel: Distribution of Max Drawdowns vs. Sharpe Ratios across all scrambled regime sequences.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    if isinstance(cpcv_source, CPCVResult):
        cpcv_res = cpcv_source
    else:
        splitter = CPCVSplitter(n_groups=n_groups)
        cpcv_res = splitter.scramble_timelines(cpcv_source)

    eq_df = cpcv_res.equity_curves
    n_total_paths = eq_df.shape[1]
    x_vals = list(eq_df.index)

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=1,
        cols=2,
        column_widths=[0.64, 0.36],
        subplot_titles=(
            f"Combinatorial Regime-Scrambled Equity Timelines ({n_total_paths} Paths)",
            "Path Survival: Sharpe vs. Max Drawdown",
        ),
        horizontal_spacing=0.08,
    )

    # Plot up to max_paths_display individual scrambled trajectories
    step = max(1, n_total_paths // max_paths_display)
    for col in eq_df.columns[::step]:
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=eq_df[col],
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": hex_to_rgba(palette.violet, 0.18), "width": 1},
                hoverinfo="skip",
                showlegend=False,
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

    # 10th-90th percentile envelope of scrambled timelines
    q10 = eq_df.quantile(0.10, axis=1)
    q90 = eq_df.quantile(0.90, axis=1)
    median_eq = eq_df.median(axis=1)

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=q90,
            mode="lines",
            line={"width": 0},
            showlegend=False,
            hoverinfo="skip",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=q10,
            mode="lines",
            line={"width": 0},
            fill="tonexty",
            fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.violet, 0.22),
            name="10th–90th Scrambled Band",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=median_eq,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 2.5},
            name="Median Combinatorial Path",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )

    if cpcv_res.historical_equity is not None:
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=list(cpcv_res.historical_equity.index),
                y=cpcv_res.historical_equity.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.amber, "width": 2.8},
                name="Chronological Historical Path",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

    # Right panel: Max Drawdown vs Sharpe scatter across scrambled timelines
    mdds = cpcv_res.max_drawdowns.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    srs = cpcv_res.sharpe_ratios.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=mdds,
            y=srs,
            mode="markers",
            marker={
                "size": 8,
                "color": srs,
                "colorscale": "Viridis",
                "showscale": False,
                "opacity": 0.85,
                "line": {"width": 0.5, "color": palette.bg_primary},
            },
            name="Scrambled Realizations",
            hovertemplate="Max Drawdown: %{x:.2%}<br>Sharpe Ratio: %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=2,
    )

    survival_rate = float(np.mean(srs > 0.0))
    median_mdd = float(np.median(mdds))
    subtitle = (
        f"Regime Blocks: {cpcv_res.n_groups} | "
        f"Survival Rate (SR > 0): {survival_rate:.1%} | "
        f"Median Scrambled Sharpe: {float(np.median(srs)):.2f} | "
        f"Median Scrambled Max DD: {median_mdd:.2%}"
    )

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=500)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Timeline Step / Date", row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Cumulative Equity (1.0 = Initial)", row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Max Drawdown (%)", tickformat=".0%", row=1, col=2)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Annualized Sharpe Ratio", row=1, col=2)
    return fig
