Two-panel visualization of Meucci's Entropy Pooling: - Panel 1 (Left): Comparative probability vector profile displaying the original equal-weight prior probabilities p against the solved posterior probabilities x*, annotated with KL-divergence and Effective Number of Scenarios (ENS). - Panel 2 (Right): Prior vs. Posterior probability-weighted return density (when scenario_data or scenario returns are supplied) or Lorenz probability concentration curve.

def plot_entropy_pooling(
    entropy_result: EntropyResult,
    scenario_data: ScenarioMarketData | np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    sort_by_posterior: bool = True,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Entropy Pooling: Prior vs. Posterior Probability & Return Density",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Two-panel visualization of Meucci's Entropy Pooling:
    - Panel 1 (Left): Comparative probability vector profile displaying the original
      equal-weight prior probabilities p against the solved posterior probabilities x*,
      annotated with KL-divergence and Effective Number of Scenarios (ENS).
    - Panel 2 (Right): Prior vs. Posterior probability-weighted return density (when
      `scenario_data` or scenario returns are supplied) or Lorenz probability concentration curve.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    prior = np.asarray(entropy_result.prior, dtype=np.float64)
    posterior = np.asarray(entropy_result.weights, dtype=np.float64)
    M = len(posterior)

    # Effective Number of Scenarios: ENS = exp(-sum(x_i * ln(x_i)))
    safe_post = np.where(posterior > 1e-16, posterior, 1e-16)
    entropy_val = -float(np.sum(posterior * np.log(safe_post)))
    ens = float(np.exp(entropy_val))
    ens_ratio = ens / max(1, M)

    has_returns = scenario_data is not None

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=1,
        cols=2,
        subplot_titles=(
            "Scenario Probability Profile (Prior p vs. Posterior x*)",
            "View-Shifted Return Density (Prior vs. Posterior)"
            if has_returns
            else "Cumulative Probability Concentration (Lorenz Curve)",
        ),
        horizontal_spacing=0.10,
    )

    if sort_by_posterior:
        order = np.argsort(posterior)[::-1]
        post_plot = posterior[order]
        prior_plot = prior[order]
        x_label = "Scenario Rank (Sorted by Posterior Weight x*)"
    else:
        post_plot = posterior
        prior_plot = prior
        x_label = "Scenario Index (m = 0 ... M-1)"

    x_idx = np.arange(M)

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_idx,
            y=post_plot,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.violet, "width": 2.2},
            fill="tozeroy",
            fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.violet, 0.30),
            name="Posterior Probability (x*)",
            hovertemplate="Rank/Idx: %{x}<br>Posterior x*: %{y:.5f}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_idx,
            y=prior_plot,
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 2, "dash": "dash"},
            name=f"Uniform Prior (1/M = {1.0 / max(1, M):.4f})",
            hovertemplate="Prior p: %{y:.5f}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )

    # Panel 2: Return Density shift if scenario_data is provided, else Lorenz concentration curve
    if scenario_data is not None:
        if isinstance(scenario_data, ScenarioMarketData):
            cum_asset_rets = scenario_data.get_cumulative_returns().astype(np.float64)
            N = cum_asset_rets.shape[1]
            if asset_weights is None:
                w = np.full(N, 1.0 / N)
            elif isinstance(asset_weights, pd.Series):
                w = (
                    asset_weights.reindex(scenario_data.asset_names)
                    .fillna(0.0)
                    .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
                )
            else:
                w = np.asarray(asset_weights, dtype=np.float64)
            scen_returns = cum_asset_rets @ w
        elif isinstance(scenario_data, pd.Series):
            scen_returns = scenario_data.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        else:
            arr = np.asarray(scenario_data, dtype=np.float64)
            scen_returns = arr if arr.ndim == 1 else np.mean(arr, axis=1)

        x_prior, y_prior = compute_kde_1d(scen_returns, weights=prior, n_points=250)
        x_post, y_post = compute_kde_1d(scen_returns, weights=posterior, n_points=250)

        prior_mean = float(np.dot(scen_returns, prior))
        post_mean = float(np.dot(scen_returns, posterior))

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_prior,
                y=y_prior,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 2.2, "dash": "dash"},
                fill="tozeroy",
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.emerald, 0.16),
                name=f"Prior Density (Mean={prior_mean:.2%})",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_post,
                y=y_post,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.violet, "width": 2.8},
                fill="tozeroy",
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.violet, 0.28),
                name=f"Posterior Density (Mean={post_mean:.2%})",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_vline(
            x=prior_mean,
            line_dash="dash",
            line_color=palette.emerald,
            line_width=1.8,
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_vline(
            x=post_mean,
            line_dash="solid",
            line_color=palette.violet,
            line_width=2.2,
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.update_xaxes(
            title_text="Cumulative Scenario Return", tickformat=".1%", row=1, col=2
        )
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Probability Density", row=1, col=2)
    else:
        sorted_post = np.sort(posterior)[::-1]
        cum_post = np.cumsum(sorted_post)
        cum_prior = np.cumsum(np.sort(prior)[::-1])
        pct_scenarios = np.arange(1, M + 1) / M

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=pct_scenarios,
                y=cum_post,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.violet, "width": 2.5},
                name="Posterior Concentration",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=pct_scenarios,
                y=cum_prior,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 2, "dash": "dash"},
                name="Uniform Prior Diagonal",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )
        fig.update_xaxes(
            title_text="Fraction of Scenarios", tickformat=".0%", row=1, col=2
        )
        fig.update_yaxes(
            title_text="Cumulative Probability Mass", tickformat=".0%", row=1, col=2
        )

    fig.update_xaxes(title_text=x_label, row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Scenario Probability Weight", row=1, col=1)

    subtitle = (
        f"KL Divergence: {entropy_result.kl_divergence:.4f} | "
        f"Effective Scenarios (ENS): {ens:.1f} / {M} ({ens_ratio:.1%}) | "
        f"Solver Converged: {entropy_result.success}"
    )
    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=500)
    return fig

Supports both: - Historical Mode (BacktestResult or pd.Series + GMMRegimeGenerator or regime probability DataFrame) - Synthetic Multiverse Mode (ScenarioMarketData with features['regime_states'])

def plot_regime_transitions(
    equity_or_scenarios: BacktestResult | pd.Series | ScenarioMarketData,
    gmm_or_probs: GMMRegimeGenerator | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray | None = None,
    market_data: MarketData | None = None,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Macro Regime Transition Overlay & State Probabilities",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Plots the portfolio equity curve against the real-time probability (p_k) of operating
    in each Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) macro regime (e.g., Bull/Low-Vol vs. Bear/High-Vol).
    Supports both:
    - Historical Mode (`BacktestResult` or `pd.Series` + `GMMRegimeGenerator` or regime probability DataFrame)
    - Synthetic Multiverse Mode (`ScenarioMarketData` with `features['regime_states']`)
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    regime_colors = [
        palette.emerald,
        palette.amber,
        palette.crimson,
        palette.violet,
        palette.cyan,
    ]

    # Case 1: Synthetic Multiverse ScenarioMarketData
    if isinstance(equity_or_scenarios, ScenarioMarketData):
        scen = equity_or_scenarios
        equity_paths, timestamps = extract_equity_paths(
            scen, asset_weights=asset_weights
        )
        x_vals = list(timestamps)
        M, T = equity_paths.shape

        if "regime_states" in scen.features:
            states_sim = scen.features["regime_states"][:, :, 0].astype(int)  # (M, T)
            unique_regimes = sorted(np.unique(states_sim).tolist())
            k_eff = max(len(unique_regimes), int(np.max(states_sim)) + 1)
            probs_arr = np.zeros((T, k_eff), dtype=np.float64)
            for k in range(k_eff):
                probs_arr[:, k] = np.mean(states_sim == k, axis=0)
            labels = (
                gmm_or_probs.regime_labels
                if isinstance(gmm_or_probs, GMMRegimeGenerator)
                and gmm_or_probs.regime_labels
                else [
                    "Bull / Low-Vol"
                    if k == 0
                    else ("Bear / High-Vol" if k == k_eff - 1 else f"Regime {k}")
                    for k in range(k_eff)
                ]
            )
            regime_probs_df = pd.DataFrame(probs_arr, index=timestamps, columns=labels)
        elif isinstance(gmm_or_probs, pd.DataFrame):
            regime_probs_df = gmm_or_probs
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                "ScenarioMarketData does not contain 'regime_states' in features; pass a fitted GMMRegimeGenerator or regime probabilities."
            )

        fig = make_subplots(
            rows=2,
            cols=1,
            shared_xaxes=True,
            row_heights=[0.62, 0.38],
            vertical_spacing=0.07,
            subplot_titles=(
                "Simulated Equity Trajectory (Median & 10th–90th Cone)",
                "Cross-Sectional Regime Probability p_k(t) Across Synthetic Paths",
            ),
        )

        q10, q50, q90 = weighted_quantiles(equity_paths, [0.10, 0.50, 0.90])
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals, y=q90, mode="lines", line={"width": 0}, showlegend=False
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=q10,
                mode="lines",
                line={"width": 0},
                fill="tonexty",
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(palette.cyan, 0.22),
                name="10th–90th Equity Cone",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=q50,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.cyan, "width": 2.8},
                name="Median Portfolio Equity",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

        for idx, col in enumerate(regime_probs_df.columns):
            c_hex = regime_colors[idx % len(regime_colors)]
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=x_vals,
                    y=regime_probs_df[col],
                    mode="lines",
                    stackgroup="regimes",
                    line={"color": c_hex, "width": 1.2},
                    fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(c_hex, 0.55),
                    name=str(col),
                    hovertemplate=f"{col}: %{{y:.1%}}<extra></extra>",
                ),
                row=2,
                col=1,
            )

        apply_plotly_theme(
            fig,
            theme=theme,
            title=title,
            subtitle=f"Dynamic Markov regime proportions across {M:,} simulated paths",
            height=580,
        )
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Portfolio Equity", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_yaxes(
            title_text="Regime Prob p_k(t)",
            tickformat=".0%",
            range=[0, 1],
            row=2,
            col=1,
        )
        fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Simulation Horizon", row=2, col=1)
        return fig

    # Case 2: Historical BacktestResult or Equity Series
    equity_series = (
        equity_or_scenarios.equity_curve
        if isinstance(equity_or_scenarios, BacktestResult)
        else pd.Series(equity_or_scenarios)
    )

    if isinstance(gmm_or_probs, GMMRegimeGenerator):
        if market_data is not None:
            regime_probs_df = gmm_or_probs.predict_regime_probs(market_data)
        elif gmm_or_probs.historical_regime_probs is not None:
            regime_probs_df = gmm_or_probs.historical_regime_probs
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                "GMMRegimeGenerator must be fitted or `market_data` provided."
            )
    elif isinstance(gmm_or_probs, pd.DataFrame):
        regime_probs_df = gmm_or_probs
    elif isinstance(gmm_or_probs, np.ndarray):
        gmm_or_probs.shape[1] if gmm_or_probs.ndim == 2 else 1
        probs_2d = (
            gmm_or_probs
            if gmm_or_probs.ndim == 2
            else np.column_stack([1.0 - gmm_or_probs, gmm_or_probs])
        )
        regime_probs_df = pd.DataFrame(
            probs_2d,
            index=equity_series.index[: len(probs_2d)],
            columns=[f"Regime {k}" for k in range(probs_2d.shape[1])],
        )
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            "Provide `gmm_or_probs` as a fitted `GMMRegimeGenerator`, DataFrame, or 2D array."
        )

    common_idx = equity_series.index.intersection(regime_probs_df.index)
    if len(common_idx) == 0:
        # Align by position if indices differ in type
        min_len = min(len(equity_series), len(regime_probs_df))
        eq_aligned = equity_series.iloc[-min_len:]
        probs_aligned = regime_probs_df.iloc[-min_len:].set_index(eq_aligned.index)
    else:
        eq_aligned = equity_series.loc[common_idx]
        probs_aligned = regime_probs_df.loc[common_idx]

    x_vals = list(eq_aligned.index)
    dominant_regime = np.argmax(probs_aligned.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64), axis=1)

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=2,
        cols=1,
        shared_xaxes=True,
        row_heights=[0.62, 0.38],
        vertical_spacing=0.07,
        subplot_titles=(
            "Portfolio Equity Curve with Dominant Macro Regime Shading",
            "Real-Time Posterior Regime Probabilities p_k(t)",
        ),
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=x_vals,
            y=eq_aligned.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": palette.text_primary, "width": 2.6},
            name="Portfolio Equity",
            hovertemplate="Equity: %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )

    # Shade contiguous dominant regime segments on the top equity chart
    if len(x_vals) > 1:
        seg_start = 0
        for t in range(1, len(x_vals) + 1):
            if t == len(x_vals) or dominant_regime[t] != dominant_regime[seg_start]:
                reg_id = int(dominant_regime[seg_start])
                c_hex = regime_colors[reg_id % len(regime_colors)]
                x0 = x_vals[seg_start]
                x1 = x_vals[min(t, len(x_vals) - 1)]
                fig.add_vrect(
                    x0=x0,
                    x1=x1,
                    fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(c_hex, 0.16),
                    line_width=0,
                    layer="below",
                    row=1,
                    col=1,
                )
                seg_start = t

    # Bottom panel: Stacked area chart of real-time regime probabilities p_k(t)
    for idx, col in enumerate(probs_aligned.columns):
        c_hex = regime_colors[idx % len(regime_colors)]
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=probs_aligned[col].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
                mode="lines",
                stackgroup="prob_stack",
                line={"color": c_hex, "width": 1.2},
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(c_hex, 0.55),
                name=str(col),
                hovertemplate=f"{col}: %{{y:.1%}}<extra></extra>",
            ),
            row=2,
            col=1,
        )

    regime_shares = probs_aligned.mean(axis=0)
    share_str = " | ".join(f"{col}: {val:.1%}" for col, val in regime_shares.items())

    apply_plotly_theme(
        fig,
        theme=theme,
        title=title,
        subtitle=f"Average Regime Occupancy — {share_str}",
        height=580,
    )
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Cumulative Equity", row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(
        title_text="Probability p_k(t)", tickformat=".0%", range=[0, 1], row=2, col=1
    )
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Date", row=2, col=1)
    return fig

def plot_multi_universe_frontier(
    expected_returns: pd.Series | np.ndarray | None = None,
    cov_matrix: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray | None = None,
    scenario_data: ScenarioMarketData | None = None,
    allocator_or_pipeline: BaseAllocator | StrategyPipeline | None = None,
    optimal_portfolios: OptimizationResult
    | Sequence[OptimizationResult]
    | pd.DataFrame
    | None = None,
    n_random_portfolios: int = 400,
    max_scenario_solves: int = 80,
    risk_free_rate: float = 0.0,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Multi-Universe Efficient Frontier & Optimal Allocation Cloud",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Renders a risk/return scatter plot combining:
    1. The parametric Markowitz Efficient Frontier curve (and individual asset coordinates).
    2. A Random Dirichlet Portfolio Cloud colored by Sharpe ratio.
    3. A Multi-Universe Optimal Allocation Cloud generated across synthetic realities
       (`ScenarioMarketData` + `allocator_or_pipeline` or precomputed `optimal_portfolios`).
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    ann_factor = 252.0

    # Infer expected_returns and cov_matrix from scenario_data if not directly provided
    asset_names: list[str] = []
    if cov_matrix is not None:
        if isinstance(cov_matrix, pd.DataFrame):
            asset_names = [str(c) for c in cov_matrix.columns]
            Sigma = cov_matrix.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        else:
            Sigma = np.asarray(cov_matrix, dtype=np.float64)
            asset_names = [f"Asset_{i}" for i in range(Sigma.shape[0])]
    elif scenario_data is not None:
        asset_names = list(scenario_data.asset_names)
        mean_path_rets = np.mean(
            scenario_data.returns.astype(np.float64), axis=0
        )  # (T, N)
        Sigma = np.cov(mean_path_rets, rowvar=False) * ann_factor
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "Provide `cov_matrix` or `scenario_data` to plot the Efficient Frontier."
        )

    N = Sigma.shape[0]
    if expected_returns is not None:
        if isinstance(expected_returns, pd.Series):
            mu = (
                expected_returns.reindex(asset_names)
                .fillna(0.0)
                .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            )
        else:
            mu = np.asarray(expected_returns, dtype=np.float64)
    elif scenario_data is not None:
        mu = np.mean(scenario_data.returns.astype(np.float64), axis=(0, 1)) * ann_factor
    else:
        mu = np.sqrt(np.diag(Sigma)) * 0.6

    fig = go.Figure()

    # 1. Random Dirichlet Portfolio Cloud
    if n_random_portfolios > 0 and N >= 2:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        rand_w = rng.dirichlet(np.ones(N), size=n_random_portfolios)
        rand_rets = rand_w @ mu
        rand_vols = np.sqrt(np.einsum("mi,ij,mj->m", rand_w, Sigma, rand_w))
        rand_sharpes = (rand_rets - risk_free_rate) / np.maximum(rand_vols, 1e-12)

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=rand_vols,
                y=rand_rets,
                mode="markers",
                marker={
                    "size": 6,
                    "color": rand_sharpes,
                    "colorscale": "Tealgrn",
                    "opacity": 0.45,
                    "colorbar": {"title": "Sharpe", "thickness": 12, "len": 0.65},
                },
                name="Random Feasible Portfolios",
                hovertemplate="Vol: %{x:.2%}<br>Return: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
            )
        )

    # 2. Parametric Markowitz Efficient Frontier Curve
    if N >= 2:
        f_vols, f_rets, _ = _solve_parametric_frontier(mu, Sigma, n_points=35)
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=f_vols,
                y=f_rets,
                mode="lines",
                line={"color": palette.emerald, "width": 3},
                name="Parametric Efficient Frontier",
                hovertemplate="Frontier Vol: %{x:.2%}<br>Frontier Return: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
            )
        )

    # 3. Individual Assets
    asset_vols = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.diag(Sigma), 0.0))
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=asset_vols,
            y=mu,
            mode="markers+text",
            text=asset_names,
            textposition="top center",
            textfont={"size": 10, "color": palette.text_secondary},
            marker={
                "size": 10,
                "symbol": "diamond",
                "color": palette.cyan,
                "line": {"width": 1.5, "color": palette.bg_primary},
            },
            name="Individual Assets",
            hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>Vol: %{x:.2%}<br>Expected Return: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

    # 4. Multi-Universe Optimal Allocation Cloud across Synthetic Realities
    sim_vols: list[float] = []
    sim_rets: list[float] = []

    if scenario_data is not None:
        M_paths = min(scenario_data.n_paths, max_scenario_solves)
        for m in range(M_paths):
            path_rets = scenario_data.returns[m].astype(np.float64)  # (T, N)
            mu_m = np.mean(path_rets, axis=0) * ann_factor
            cov_m = np.cov(path_rets, rowvar=False) * ann_factor
            if cov_m.ndim == 0:
                cov_m = np.array([[float(cov_m)]])

            w_m: np.ndarray | None = None
            if isinstance(allocator_or_pipeline, StrategyPipeline):
                path_md = scenario_data.get_path(m)
                w_ser = allocator_or_pipeline.generate_weights(path_md)
                w_m = w_ser.reindex(asset_names).fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            elif isinstance(allocator_or_pipeline, BaseAllocator):
                path_md = scenario_data.get_path(m)
                cov_df = pd.DataFrame(cov_m, index=asset_names, columns=asset_names)
                mu_ser = pd.Series(mu_m, index=asset_names)
                try:
                    opt_res = allocator_or_pipeline.allocate(
                        data=path_md, cov_matrix=cov_df, expected_returns=mu_ser
                    )
                    w_m = (
                        opt_res.weights.reindex(asset_names)
                        .fillna(0.0)
                        .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
                    )
                except (ValueError, RuntimeError, np.linalg.LinAlgError):
                    w_m = None
            else:
                # Default: compute min-variance / tangency allocation on scenario m
                inv_diag = 1.0 / np.maximum(np.diag(cov_m), 1e-8)
                w_m = inv_diag / np.sum(inv_diag)

            if w_m is not None and np.sum(w_m) > 0:
                w_m = w_m / np.sum(w_m)
                # Plot scenario-optimal portfolio evaluated under scenario m's realized dynamics
                sim_vols.append(float(np.sqrt(max(float(w_m.T @ cov_m @ w_m), 0.0))))
                sim_rets.append(float(w_m @ mu_m))

    if len(sim_vols) > 0:
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=sim_vols,
                y=sim_rets,
                mode="markers",
                marker={
                    "size": 9,
                    "color": palette.violet,
                    "opacity": 0.82,
                    "symbol": "circle",
                    "line": {"width": 1, "color": palette.text_primary},
                },
                name=f"Multi-Universe Optimal Cloud ({len(sim_vols)} Realities)",
                hovertemplate="Scenario Optimal Vol: %{x:.2%}<br>Scenario Optimal Return: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
            )
        )

    # 5. Highlighted Optimal Portfolio(s)
    if optimal_portfolios is not None:
        opt_list: list[tuple[str, np.ndarray]] = []
        if isinstance(optimal_portfolios, OptimizationResult):
            w_arr = (
                optimal_portfolios.weights.reindex(asset_names)
                .fillna(0.0)
                .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            )
            opt_list.append(
                (str(getattr(optimal_portfolios, "status", "Optimal Portfolio")), w_arr)
            )
        elif isinstance(optimal_portfolios, pd.DataFrame):
            for idx_name, row in optimal_portfolios.iterrows():
                opt_list.append(
                    (
                        str(idx_name),
                        row.reindex(asset_names).fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
                    )
                )
        else:
            for i, opt in enumerate(optimal_portfolios):
                w_arr = (
                    opt.weights.reindex(asset_names)
                    .fillna(0.0)
                    .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
                )
                opt_list.append((f"{opt.status} ({i+1})", w_arr))

        for label, w_arr in opt_list:
            p_vol = float(np.sqrt(max(float(w_arr.T @ Sigma @ w_arr), 0.0)))
            p_ret = float(w_arr @ mu)
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=[p_vol],
                    y=[p_ret],
                    mode="markers",
                    marker={
                        "size": 15,
                        "symbol": "star",
                        "color": palette.amber,
                        "line": {"width": 1.5, "color": palette.bg_primary},
                    },
                    name=label,
                    hovertemplate=f"<b>{label}</b><br>Vol: %{{x:.2%}}<br>Return: %{{y:.2%}}<extra></extra>",
                )
            )

    subtitle = f"Universe of {N} assets"
    if len(sim_vols) > 0:
        subtitle += f" | {len(sim_vols)} synthetic optimal allocations rendered"

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=540)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Annualized Volatility (σ)", tickformat=".1%")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Annualized Expected Return (μ)", tickformat=".1%")
    return fig

def plot_weight_drift_turnover(
    backtest_result: BacktestResult | pd.DataFrame,
    market_data: MarketData | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Asset Weight Drift & Rebalance Turnover Dynamics",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Plots a two-panel view of portfolio allocation mechanics over time:
    - Top Panel: Stacked area chart of asset weights drifting naturally due to daily
      market movements and snapping back during rebalancing events.
    - Bottom Panel: Bar chart of two-way portfolio turnover at each rebalance event
      alongside cumulative turnover.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)
    drifted_df, turnover_series = reconstruct_drifted_weights(
        backtest_result, market_data=market_data
    )

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=2,
        cols=1,
        shared_xaxes=True,
        row_heights=[0.66, 0.34],
        vertical_spacing=0.07,
        subplot_titles=(
            "Drifted Asset Weights & Rebalance Snap-Backs",
            "Rebalance Two-Way Turnover (∑ |Δw_i|)",
        ),
    )

    x_vals = list(drifted_df.index)
    for idx, asset in enumerate(drifted_df.columns):
        c_hex = palette.categorical[idx % len(palette.categorical)]
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=x_vals,
                y=drifted_df[asset].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
                mode="lines",
                stackgroup="weights",
                line={"color": c_hex, "width": 1.0},
                fillcolor=hex_to_rgba(c_hex, 0.72),
                name=str(asset),
                hovertemplate=f"<b>{asset}</b>: %{{y:.2%}}<extra></extra>",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=1,
        )

    # Filter non-zero rebalance events for cleaner bar chart rendering
    reb_events = turnover_series[turnover_series > 1e-5]
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x=list(reb_events.index),
            y=reb_events.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            marker={
                "color": palette.amber,
                "line": {"color": palette.amber, "width": 1},
            },
            name="Rebalance Turnover",
            hovertemplate="Date: %{x}<br>Turnover: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=2,
        col=1,
    )

    total_turnover = (
        float(turnover_series.iloc[1:].sum()) if len(turnover_series) > 1 else 0.0
    )
    n_rebalances = (
        int((turnover_series.iloc[1:] > 1e-5).sum()) if len(turnover_series) > 1 else 0
    )

    subtitle = (
        f"Rebalance Events: {n_rebalances} | "
        f"Cumulative Post-Init Turnover: {total_turnover:.1%} | "
        f"Avg Turnover / Rebalance: {(total_turnover / max(1, n_rebalances)):.2%}"
    )

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=580)
    fig.update_yaxes(
        title_text="Portfolio Weight", tickformat=".0%", range=[0.0, 1.0], row=1, col=1
    )
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Turnover (%)", tickformat=".0%", row=2, col=1)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Date", row=2, col=1)
    return fig

def plot_hierarchical_composition(
    weights_or_result: OptimizationResult | pd.Series,
    target_or_benchmark_weights: OptimizationResult | pd.Series | None = None,
    hierarchy: Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]] | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    market_data: MarketData | None = None,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Hierarchical Portfolio Composition & Target vs. Current Allocation",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Left Panel: Multi-level Treemap displaying hierarchical portfolio structure
      (e.g., Portfolio -> Sector/Cluster -> Asset), resolving hierarchy from explicit
      `hierarchy` mapping, `MarketData.cross_sectional`, `OptimizationResult.metadata['clusters']`,
      or flat fallback.
    Right Panel: Grouped horizontal comparison bar chart of Current/Optimized vs. Target/Benchmark weights.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    if isinstance(weights_or_result, OptimizationResult):
        w_series = weights_or_result.weights.copy()
        meta_clusters = weights_or_result.metadata.get("clusters")
    else:
        w_series = pd.Series(weights_or_result).copy()
        meta_clusters = None

    w_series = w_series[w_series > 1e-6]
    assets = [str(a) for a in w_series.index]

    # Resolve parent group for each asset
    parent_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    if isinstance(hierarchy, pd.DataFrame):
        col = hierarchy.columns[0]
        for a in assets:
            if a in hierarchy.index:
                parent_map[a] = str(hierarchy.loc[a, col])
    elif isinstance(hierarchy, Mapping):
        for k, v in hierarchy.items():
            if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) and not isinstance(v, str):
                parent_map[str(k)] = " / ".join(str(x) for x in v)
            else:
                parent_map[str(k)] = str(v)
    elif (
        market_data is not None
        and market_data.cross_sectional is not None
        and not market_data.cross_sectional.empty
    ):
        cs = market_data.cross_sectional
        sector_col = next(
            (
                c
                for c in cs.columns
                if "sector" in str(c).lower()
                or "group" in str(c).lower()
                or "class" in str(c).lower()
            ),
            cs.columns[0],
        )
        for a in assets:
            if a in cs.index:
                parent_map[a] = str(cs.loc[a, sector_col])
    elif isinstance(meta_clusters, Mapping):
        for a in assets:
            if a in meta_clusters:
                parent_map[a] = str(meta_clusters[a])

    # Build Treemap nodes (Root -> Group -> Asset)
    root_label = "Portfolio"
    ids: list[str] = [root_label]
    labels: list[str] = [root_label]
    parents: list[str] = [""]
    values: list[float] = [float(w_series.sum())]

    if parent_map:
        group_totals: dict[str, float] = {}
        for k_asset, val in w_series.items():
            g = parent_map.get(str(k_asset), "Other")
            group_totals[g] = group_totals.get(g, 0.0) + float(val)

        for g, g_val in group_totals.items():
            g_id = f"{root_label}/{g}"
            ids.append(g_id)
            labels.append(g)
            parents.append(root_label)
            values.append(g_val)

        for k_asset, val in w_series.items():
            a_str = str(k_asset)
            g = parent_map.get(a_str, "Other")
            g_id = f"{root_label}/{g}"
            ids.append(f"{g_id}/{a_str}")
            labels.append(a_str)
            parents.append(g_id)
            values.append(float(val))
    else:
        for k_asset, val in w_series.items():
            a_str = str(k_asset)
            ids.append(f"{root_label}/{a_str}")
            labels.append(a_str)
            parents.append(root_label)
            values.append(float(val))

    # Resolve target / benchmark comparison weights
    if target_or_benchmark_weights is not None:
        if isinstance(target_or_benchmark_weights, OptimizationResult):
            bench_w = target_or_benchmark_weights.weights.reindex(
                w_series.index
            ).fillna(0.0)
        else:
            bench_w = (
                pd.Series(target_or_benchmark_weights)
                .reindex(w_series.index)
                .fillna(0.0)
            )
        bench_label = "Target / Benchmark Weight"
    else:
        bench_w = pd.Series(1.0 / max(1, len(w_series)), index=w_series.index)
        bench_label = "Equal-Weight Benchmark (1/N)"

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=1,
        cols=2,
        column_widths=[0.54, 0.46],
        specs=[[{"type": "domain"}, {"type": "xy"}]],
        subplot_titles=(
            "Hierarchical Composition Treemap",
            "Current vs. Target / Benchmark Allocation",
        ),
        horizontal_spacing=0.08,
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Treemap(
            ids=ids,
            labels=labels,
            parents=parents,
            values=values,
            branchvalues="total",
            textinfo="label+percent root",
            hovertemplate="<b>%{label}</b><br>Weight: %{value:.2%}<extra></extra>",
            marker={
                "colorscale": "Tealgrn",
                "line": {"width": 1.5, "color": palette.bg_primary},
            },
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )

    sorted_idx = w_series.sort_values(ascending=True).index
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            y=[str(a) for a in sorted_idx],
            x=w_series.loc[sorted_idx].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            orientation="h",
            marker={"color": palette.emerald},
            name="Optimized Weight",
            hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>Optimized: %{x:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=2,
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            y=[str(a) for a in sorted_idx],
            x=bench_w.loc[sorted_idx].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            orientation="h",
            marker={"color": palette.amber},
            name=bench_label,
            hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>Target/Bench: %{x:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=2,
    )

    eff_n = float(1.0 / np.sum(np.square(w_series.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64))))
    subtitle = (
        f"Active Assets: {len(w_series)} | "
        f"Effective Number of Bets (1 / ∑w²): {eff_n:.2f} | "
        f"Max Single Weight: {float(w_series.max()):.1%}"
    )

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=520)
    fig.update_layout(barmode="group")
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Allocation Weight (%)", tickformat=".0%", row=1, col=2)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Asset", row=1, col=2)
    return fig

def plot_risk_contributions(
    weights_or_result: OptimizationResult | pd.Series | np.ndarray,
    cov_matrix: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    target_risk_budgets: pd.Series | np.ndarray | None = None,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Capital Allocation vs. Component Risk Contributions",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Compares Capital Weights (w_i), Percentage Component Risk Contributions
    (PCRC_i = w_i * (Sigma w)_i / (w^T Sigma w)), and Target Risk Budgets (b_i).
    Crucial for validating Risk Parity, Risk Budgeting, HRP, and HERC strategies.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    w: pd.Series | np.ndarray
    if isinstance(weights_or_result, OptimizationResult):
        w = weights_or_result.weights
        if (
            target_risk_budgets is None
            and "target_budgets" in weights_or_result.metadata
        ):
            target_risk_budgets = np.asarray(
                weights_or_result.metadata["target_budgets"], dtype=np.float64
            )
    else:
        w = weights_or_result

    rc_df = compute_risk_contributions(w, cov_matrix)
    assets = [str(a) for a in rc_df.index]
    N = len(assets)

    if target_risk_budgets is not None:
        if isinstance(target_risk_budgets, pd.Series):
            budgets = (
                target_risk_budgets.reindex(rc_df.index)
                .fillna(1.0 / N)
                .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            )
        else:
            budgets = np.asarray(target_risk_budgets, dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        budgets = np.full(N, 1.0 / max(1, N), dtype=np.float64)

    fig = go.Figure()

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x=assets,
            y=rc_df["weight"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            name="Capital Weight (w_i)",
            marker={"color": palette.cyan},
            hovertemplate="<b>%{x}</b><br>Capital Weight: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x=assets,
            y=rc_df["pcrc"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            name="Risk Contribution (PCRC_i)",
            marker={"color": palette.coral},
            hovertemplate="<b>%{x}</b><br>Risk Contribution: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=assets,
            y=budgets,
            mode="lines+markers",
            line={"color": palette.amber, "width": 2.5, "dash": "dash"},
            marker={"size": 9, "symbol": "diamond", "color": palette.amber},
            name="Target Risk Budget (b_i)",
            hovertemplate="<b>%{x}</b><br>Target Budget: %{y:.2%}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

    pcrc_vals = np.clip(rc_df["pcrc"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64), 1e-12, None)
    eff_risk_bets = float(1.0 / np.sum(np.square(pcrc_vals)))
    port_vol = float(np.sum(rc_df["crc"]))

    subtitle = (
        f"Portfolio Volatility: {port_vol:.2%} | "
        f"Effective Number of Risk Bets (ENCB): {eff_risk_bets:.2f} / {N} | "
        f"Max Risk Concentration: {float(np.max(pcrc_vals)):.1%}"
    )

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=480)
    fig.update_layout(barmode="group")
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Asset")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Share of Capital / Risk (%)", tickformat=".0%")
    return fig

def plot_correlation_and_periodic_returns(
    market_data_or_cov: MarketData | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    portfolio_returns: BacktestResult | pd.Series | None = None,
    cluster_order: bool = True,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Asset Correlation Matrix & Monthly Periodic Return Heatmap",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Two-panel diagnostic figure:
    - Left Panel: Asset Return Correlation Matrix Heatmap (optionally quasi-diagonalized
      via hierarchical clustering so correlated asset blocks stand out visually).
    - Right Panel: Monthly Periodic Return Table Heatmap (Jan-Dec across x-axis,
      Years on y-axis) to visualize seasonal performance and annual compounding.
    """
    get_theme(theme)

    # Extract correlation matrix
    if isinstance(market_data_or_cov, MarketData):
        rets_df = market_data_or_cov.get_returns()
        corr_df = rets_df.corr()
        if portfolio_returns is None:
            portfolio_returns = rets_df.mean(axis=1)
    elif isinstance(market_data_or_cov, pd.DataFrame):
        # Check if it's already a square covariance/correlation matrix or a time series of prices/returns
        if market_data_or_cov.shape[0] == market_data_or_cov.shape[1] and list(
            market_data_or_cov.index
        ) == list(market_data_or_cov.columns):
            corr_np = cov_to_corr(market_data_or_cov.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64))
            corr_df = pd.DataFrame(
                corr_np,
                index=market_data_or_cov.index,
                columns=market_data_or_cov.columns,
            )
        else:
            corr_df = market_data_or_cov.pct_change().dropna().corr()
    else:
        corr_np = cov_to_corr(np.asarray(market_data_or_cov, dtype=np.float64))
        names = [f"Asset_{i}" for i in range(corr_np.shape[0])]
        corr_df = pd.DataFrame(corr_np, index=names, columns=names)

    if cluster_order and corr_df.shape[0] > 2:
        try:
            dist = np.sqrt(
                np.clip(0.5 * (1.0 - corr_df.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)), 0.0, 1.0)
            )
            np.fill_diagonal(dist, 0.0)
            link = sch.linkage(ssd.squareform(dist, checks=False), method="single")
            leaves = sch.leaves_list(link)
            corr_df = corr_df.iloc[leaves, leaves]
        except (ValueError, np.linalg.LinAlgError):
            corr_df = corr_df.copy()

    # Extract portfolio returns for the monthly heatmap
    ret_series: pd.Series | None = None
    if isinstance(portfolio_returns, BacktestResult):
        ret_series = portfolio_returns.returns.dropna()
    elif isinstance(portfolio_returns, pd.Series):
        ret_series = portfolio_returns.dropna()

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=1,
        cols=2,
        column_widths=[0.46, 0.54],
        subplot_titles=(
            "Quasi-Diagonalized Asset Correlation Heatmap"
            if cluster_order
            else "Asset Correlation Matrix Heatmap",
            "Monthly Periodic Returns (%) — Seasonal Performance",
        ),
        horizontal_spacing=0.10,
    )

    corr_vals = corr_df.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    corr_labels = [str(c) for c in corr_df.columns]

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Heatmap(
            z=corr_vals,
            x=corr_labels,
            y=corr_labels,
            zmin=-1.0,
            zmax=1.0,
            colorscale="RdBu_r",
            text=np.round(corr_vals, 2),
            texttemplate="%{text:.2f}",
            showscale=False,
            hovertemplate="<b>%{x} vs %{y}</b><br>Correlation: %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )

    # Compute Monthly Return Grid (Years x Jan..Dec)
    if ret_series is not None and len(ret_series) > 0:
        if not isinstance(ret_series.index, pd.DatetimeIndex):
            # Create synthetic daily business dates starting 2022-01-03 if RangeIndex
            ret_series = ret_series.copy()
            ret_series.index = pd.bdate_range("2022-01-03", periods=len(ret_series))

        monthly = (1.0 + ret_series).resample("ME").prod() - 1.0
        m_dt_idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(monthly.index)
        df_m = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "Year": m_dt_idx.year,
                "Month": m_dt_idx.month,
                "Return": monthly.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),
            }
        )
        pivot = df_m.pivot(index="Year", columns="Month", values="Return")
        for m in range(1, 13):
            if m not in pivot.columns:
                pivot[m] = np.nan
        pivot = pivot[list(range(1, 13))]
        pivot.columns = [calendar.month_abbr[m] for m in range(1, 13)]

        # Add Annual Compounded column
        annual = (1.0 + ret_series).resample("YE").prod() - 1.0
        a_dt_idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(annual.index)
        pivot["Year Total"] = [
            float(annual[a_dt_idx.year == yr].iloc[0])
            if any(a_dt_idx.year == yr)
            else np.nan
            for yr in pivot.index
        ]

        z_mat = pivot.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64) * 100.0
        text_mat = np.where(np.isfinite(z_mat), np.char.mod("%.1f%%", z_mat), "")
        y_years = [str(y) for y in pivot.index]
        x_months = list(pivot.columns)

        fig.add_trace(
            go.Heatmap(
                z=z_mat,
                x=x_months,
                y=y_years,
                colorscale="RdYlGn",
                zmid=0.0,
                text=text_mat,
                texttemplate="%{text}",
                showscale=True,
                colorbar={"title": "Ret (%)", "thickness": 12, "len": 0.75},
                hovertemplate="<b>%{y} %{x}</b><br>Return: %{z:.2f}%<extra></extra>",
            ),
            row=1,
            col=2,
        )

    avg_off_diag_corr = (
        float(
            (np.sum(corr_vals) - np.trace(corr_vals))
            / max(1, corr_vals.size - len(corr_labels))
        )
        if len(corr_labels) > 1
        else 0.0
    )
    subtitle = f"Assets: {len(corr_labels)} | Mean Pairwise Correlation: {avg_off_diag_corr:.2f}"

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, subtitle=subtitle, height=520)
    fig.update_yaxes(autorange="reversed", row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(autorange="reversed", row=1, col=2)
    return fig

def apply_plotly_theme(
    fig: Any,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str | None = None,
    subtitle: str | None = None,
    height: int | None = None,
    width: int | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """
    Applies the institutional PyAlloq layout styling to a Plotly Figure or Matplotlib Figure.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    # Check if fig is a Plotly Figure (duck-typed via update_layout)
    if hasattr(fig, "update_layout"):
        title_text = title
        if title and subtitle:
            title_text = (
                f"<b>{title}</b><br>"
                f"<span style='font-size:12px;color:{palette.text_secondary}'>{subtitle}</span>"
            )
        elif title:
            title_text = f"<b>{title}</b>"

        layout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "paper_bgcolor": palette.bg_primary,
            "plot_bgcolor": palette.bg_secondary,
            "font": {
                "family": "Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif",
                "color": palette.text_primary,
                "size": 12,
            },
            "colorway": list(palette.categorical),
            "margin": {"l": 60, "r": 40, "t": 80 if title_text else 45, "b": 55},
            "hovermode": "x unified",
            "legend": {
                "bgcolor": hex_to_rgba(
                    palette.bg_card if palette.name == "alloq_dark" else "#FFFFFF", 0.8
                ),
                "bordercolor": palette.border_color,
                "borderwidth": 1,
                "font": {"color": palette.text_primary, "size": 11},
            },
        }
        if title_text is not None:
            layout_kwargs["title"] = {
                "text": title_text,
                "x": 0.02,
                "xanchor": "left",
                "font": {"size": 17, "color": palette.text_primary},
            }
        if height is not None:
            layout_kwargs["height"] = height
        if width is not None:
            layout_kwargs["width"] = width

        fig.update_layout(**layout_kwargs)
        fig.update_xaxes(
            gridcolor=palette.grid_color,
            zerolinecolor=palette.border_color,
            linecolor=palette.border_color,
            tickfont={"color": palette.text_secondary},
            title_font={"color": palette.text_primary},
        )
        fig.update_yaxes(
            gridcolor=palette.grid_color,
            zerolinecolor=palette.border_color,
            linecolor=palette.border_color,
            tickfont={"color": palette.text_secondary},
            title_font={"color": palette.text_primary},
        )
        # Update subplot titles if present
        if hasattr(fig.layout, "annotations") and fig.layout.annotations:
            for ann in fig.layout.annotations:
                if hasattr(ann, "font") and ann.font is not None and not ann.font.color:
                    ann.font.color = palette.text_primary
        return fig

    # Matplotlib Figure fallback
    if isinstance(fig, plt.Figure):
        fig.patch.set_facecolor(palette.bg_primary)
        for ax in fig.axes:
            ax.set_facecolor(palette.bg_secondary)
            ax.tick_params(colors=palette.text_secondary)
            ax.xaxis.label.set_color(palette.text_primary)
            ax.yaxis.label.set_color(palette.text_primary)
            ax.title.set_color(palette.text_primary)
            for spine in ax.spines.values():
                spine.set_edgecolor(palette.border_color)
            ax.grid(True, color=palette.border_color, alpha=0.3, linestyle="--")
        if title:
            fig.suptitle(
                title, color=palette.text_primary, fontsize=14, fontweight="bold"
            )
        return fig

    return fig

def hex_to_rgba(hex_color: str, alpha: float = 1.0) -> str:
    """Converts a 6-digit hex string (e.g. '#10B981') into an 'rgba(r, g, b, a)' string."""
    h = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    if len(h) == 3:
        h = "".join(c * 2 for c in h)
    r, g, b = int(h[0:2], 16), int(h[2:4], 16), int(h[4:6], 16)
    return f"rgba({r}, {g}, {b}, {alpha:.3f})"

    sample_weight: ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray

Computes probability-weighted quantiles along 1D or 2D arrays. If values is 2D of shape (M, T), computes quantiles across axis=0 for each step t=0..T-1, returning an array of shape (len(quantiles), T).

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def weighted_quantiles(
    values: np.ndarray,
    quantiles: list[float] | np.ndarray,
    sample_weight: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Computes probability-weighted quantiles along 1D or 2D arrays.
    If `values` is 2D of shape (M, T), computes quantiles across axis=0 for each step t=0..T-1,
    returning an array of shape (len(quantiles), T).
    """
    q_arr = np.asarray(quantiles, dtype=np.float64)
    vals = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)

    if sample_weight is None:
        return np.quantile(vals, q_arr, axis=0)

    weights = np.asarray(sample_weight, dtype=np.float64)
    weights = weights / np.sum(weights)

    if vals.ndim == 1:
        sorter = np.argsort(vals)
        v_sorted = vals[sorter]
        w_sorted = weights[sorter]
        cdf = np.cumsum(w_sorted) - 0.5 * w_sorted
        cdf = np.clip(cdf / cdf[-1], 0.0, 1.0)
        return np.interp(q_arr, cdf, v_sorted)

    if vals.ndim == 2:
        _M, T = vals.shape
        out = np.zeros((len(q_arr), T), dtype=np.float64)
        for t in range(T):
            col = vals[:, t]
            sorter = np.argsort(col)
            v_sorted = col[sorter]
            w_sorted = weights[sorter]
            cdf = np.cumsum(w_sorted) - 0.5 * w_sorted
            cdf = np.clip(cdf / cdf[-1], 0.0, 1.0)
            out[:, t] = np.interp(q_arr, cdf, v_sorted)
        return out

    raise ValueError("`values` must be 1D or 2D.")

Computes a smooth 1D Kernel Density Estimate (supporting scenario probability weights).

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def compute_kde_1d(
    values: np.ndarray,
    weights: np.ndarray | None = None,
    n_points: int = 250,
    padding: float = 0.1,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Computes a smooth 1D Kernel Density Estimate (supporting scenario probability weights).
    """
    vals = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    mask = np.isfinite(vals)
    vals = vals[mask]
    if len(vals) < 2 or np.std(vals) < 1e-12:
        center = float(np.mean(vals)) if len(vals) > 0 else 0.0
        x_grid = np.linspace(center - 0.05, center + 0.05, n_points)
        y_grid = np.exp(-0.5 * ((x_grid - center) / 0.01) ** 2)
        return x_grid, y_grid

    vmin, vmax = float(np.min(vals)), float(np.max(vals))
    span = max(vmax - vmin, 1e-6)
    x_grid = np.linspace(vmin - padding * span, vmax + padding * span, n_points)

    w_clean = None
    if weights is not None:
        w_arr = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)[mask]
        if np.sum(w_arr) > 0:
            w_clean = w_arr / np.sum(w_arr)

    try:
        kde = gaussian_kde(vals, weights=w_clean)
        y_grid = kde(x_grid)
    except (ValueError, np.linalg.LinAlgError):
        hist, bin_edges = np.histogram(
            vals, bins=min(30, max(5, len(vals) // 5)), weights=w_clean, density=True
        )
        centers = 0.5 * (bin_edges[:-1] + bin_edges[1:])
        y_grid = np.interp(x_grid, centers, hist, left=0.0, right=0.0)

    return x_grid, y_grid

Extracts a 2D array of portfolio equity paths of shape (M, T_steps) and corresponding timestamps from a MonteCarloResult, ScenarioMarketData, DataFrame, or ndarray.

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def extract_equity_paths(
    source: MonteCarloResult | ScenarioMarketData | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, pd.Index]:
    """
    Extracts a 2D array of portfolio equity paths of shape (M, T_steps) and corresponding timestamps
    from a MonteCarloResult, ScenarioMarketData, DataFrame, or ndarray.
    """
    if isinstance(source, MonteCarloResult):
        # equity_curves in MonteCarloResult has shape (T, M) where columns are Path_0..Path_M-1
        df_eq = source.equity_curves
        return df_eq.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64).T, df_eq.index

    if isinstance(source, ScenarioMarketData):
        _M, _T, N = source.prices.shape
        if asset_weights is None:
            w = np.full(N, 1.0 / N, dtype=np.float64)
        elif isinstance(asset_weights, pd.Series):
            w = (
                asset_weights.reindex(source.asset_names)
                .fillna(0.0)
                .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            )
        else:
            w = np.asarray(asset_weights, dtype=np.float64)

        if np.sum(np.abs(w)) > 0:
            w = w / np.sum(w)

        if source.initial_prices is not None:
            init_p = np.asarray(source.initial_prices, dtype=np.float64)[None, None, :]
            rel_prices = source.prices.astype(np.float64) / init_p
            step_wealth = np.asarray(
                np.tensordot(rel_prices, w, axes=([2], [0])), dtype=np.float64
            )  # (M, T)
        else:
            step_rets = np.tensordot(
                source.returns.astype(np.float64), w, axes=([2], [0])
            )
            step_wealth = np.asarray(
                np.cumprod(1.0 + step_rets, axis=1), dtype=np.float64
            )

        return step_wealth, source.timestamps

    if isinstance(source, pd.DataFrame):
        # Convention: if columns start with "Path" or index is DatetimeIndex, shape is (T, M)
        if isinstance(source.index, pd.DatetimeIndex) or any(
            str(c).startswith("Path") or str(c).startswith("CPCV")
            for c in source.columns
        ):
            return source.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64).T, source.index
        return source.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64), source.columns

    arr = np.asarray(source, dtype=np.float64)
    if arr.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("Equity paths array must be 2D of shape (M, T).")
    return arr, pd.RangeIndex(arr.shape[1])

Computes underwater drawdown trajectories of shape (M, T) from equity paths of shape (M, T). Prepends 1.0 peak so initial drops below 1.0 are captured accurately.

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def compute_drawdown_paths(equity_paths: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Computes underwater drawdown trajectories of shape (M, T) from equity paths of shape (M, T).
    Prepends 1.0 peak so initial drops below 1.0 are captured accurately.
    """
    eq = np.asarray(equity_paths, dtype=np.float64)
    running_peaks = np.maximum.accumulate(np.maximum(eq, 1.0), axis=1)
    drawdowns = (eq - running_peaks) / np.maximum(running_peaks, 1e-12)
    return drawdowns

Computes Capital Weight, Marginal Risk Contribution (MRC), Component Risk Contribution (CRC), and Percentage Component Risk Contribution (PCRC) for a portfolio.

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def compute_risk_contributions(
    weights: pd.Series | np.ndarray,
    cov_matrix: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Computes Capital Weight, Marginal Risk Contribution (MRC), Component Risk Contribution (CRC),
    and Percentage Component Risk Contribution (PCRC) for a portfolio.
    """
    if isinstance(cov_matrix, pd.DataFrame):
        assets = list(cov_matrix.columns)
        Sigma = cov_matrix.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        Sigma = np.asarray(cov_matrix, dtype=np.float64)
        assets = [f"Asset_{i}" for i in range(Sigma.shape[0])]

    if isinstance(weights, pd.Series):
        w = weights.reindex(assets).fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)

    port_var = float(w.T @ Sigma @ w)
    port_vol = float(np.sqrt(max(port_var, 1e-16)))

    sigma_w = Sigma @ w
    mrc = sigma_w / port_vol
    crc = w * mrc
    pcrc = crc / port_vol if port_vol > 1e-12 else np.zeros_like(w)

    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "weight": w,
            "mrc": mrc,
            "crc": crc,
            "pcrc": pcrc,
        },
        index=assets,
    )

reconstruct_drifted_weights(
    backtest_result: BacktestResult | DataFrame,
    market_data: MarketData | DataFrame | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]

Reconstructs true intra-period drifted asset weights and rebalance turnover events. When market_data (or asset prices DataFrame) is provided, simulates natural market drift: w_{i, t}^- = w_{i, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{i, t}) / sum_j w_{j, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{j, t}) and snaps back to target weights on dates where the target allocation changes. Returns: (drifted_weights_df, turnover_series)

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def reconstruct_drifted_weights(
    backtest_result: BacktestResult | pd.DataFrame,
    market_data: MarketData | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """
    Reconstructs true intra-period drifted asset weights and rebalance turnover events.
    When `market_data` (or asset prices DataFrame) is provided, simulates natural market drift:
        w_{i, t}^- = w_{i, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{i, t}) / sum_j w_{j, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{j, t})
    and snaps back to target weights on dates where the target allocation changes.
    Returns:
        (drifted_weights_df, turnover_series)
    """
    if isinstance(backtest_result, BacktestResult):
        target_w = backtest_result.weights.dropna(how="all").fillna(0.0)
    else:
        target_w = backtest_result.dropna(how="all").fillna(0.0)

    if len(target_w) == 0:
        return target_w.copy(), pd.Series(dtype=float)

    prices_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None
    if isinstance(market_data, MarketData):
        prices_df = market_data.prices
    elif isinstance(market_data, pd.DataFrame):
        prices_df = market_data

    # Identify rebalance dates where target weights change (or first valid date)
    w_diff = target_w.diff().abs().sum(axis=1)
    rebalance_mask = (w_diff > 1e-7) | (np.arange(len(target_w)) == 0)

    if prices_df is None:
        turnover = w_diff.where(rebalance_mask, 0.0)
        return target_w.copy(), turnover

    common_dates = target_w.index.intersection(prices_df.index)
    if len(common_dates) < 2:
        turnover = w_diff.where(rebalance_mask, 0.0)
        return target_w.copy(), turnover

    target_aligned = target_w.loc[common_dates]
    asset_rets = (
        prices_df.reindex(columns=target_aligned.columns)
        .pct_change()
        .reindex(common_dates)
        .fillna(0.0)
    )
    reb_aligned = rebalance_mask.loc[common_dates]

    T, N = target_aligned.shape
    drifted_arr = np.zeros((T, N), dtype=np.float64)
    turnover_arr = np.zeros(T, dtype=np.float64)

    target_np = target_aligned.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    rets_np = asset_rets.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    reb_np = reb_aligned.to_numpy(dtype=bool)

    current_w = target_np[0].copy()
    drifted_arr[0] = current_w
    turnover_arr[0] = float(np.sum(np.abs(current_w)))

    for t in range(1, T):
        # Drift weights by day t's asset returns
        grown = current_w * (1.0 + rets_np[t])
        total_val = float(np.sum(grown))
        pre_rebalance_w = grown / total_val if total_val > 1e-12 else current_w

        if reb_np[t]:
            # Snap back to new target weights
            new_target = target_np[t]
            turnover_arr[t] = float(np.sum(np.abs(new_target - pre_rebalance_w)))
            current_w = new_target.copy()
        else:
            current_w = pre_rebalance_w

        drifted_arr[t] = current_w

    drifted_df = pd.DataFrame(
        drifted_arr, index=common_dates, columns=target_aligned.columns
    )
    turnover_series = pd.Series(turnover_arr, index=common_dates, name="Turnover")
    return drifted_df, turnover_series

docs.title: Building Blocks
docs.text:
PyAlloq is built around six composable building blocks. Each one has a clean, stable interface. You can swap any block independently without touching the others.

This design lets you answer questions like:

"Does Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage improve my Markowitz backtest?" "Does James-Stein return estimation help HRP more than EWMA?" "What happens if I use Almgren-Chriss costs instead of flat fees?"

...all without rewriting your backtesting code.
